`<DivergingBarChart>`, chart, category comparison. Draws bars either side of a centre line: positive against negative values, or stacked agree / disagree responses around a neutral midpoint.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. Category field.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. One signed value field, or several fields ordered from most negative to most positive.
- `series`: `string`. Field that splits rows into ordered series (long data).
- `neutral`: `string | false`. Series centred on the midline. Default: the middle one of an odd number of series.
- `percent`: `boolean`, default `false`. Normalise each row to 100% (stacked series).
- `colors`: `"polarity" | "sentiment"`, default `"polarity"`. Single series: diverging poles, or the positive / negative colours when one side is good and the other bad.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`. Row order. Default: descending by value or by the positive side; data order for dates.
- `orientation`: `"auto" | "horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `"auto"`. Horizontal, except vertical for a single series over dates.
- `labels`: `boolean`. Values at bar ends (single) or inside segments (stacked). Default: on when there is room.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for series keys.

```json
{"type":"diverging-bar-chart","data":[{"city":"Austin","change":21.3},{"city":"Phoenix","change":11.2},{"city":"Seattle","change":8.1},{"city":"Chicago","change":-2.9},{"city":"San Francisco","change":-7.4},{"city":"St. Louis","change":-11.6}],"x":"city","y":"change","format":"{value}%","height":260,"title":"Austin's population grew 21.3% between 2010 and 2020","subtitle":"Population change, 2010 to 2020","note":"Illustrative figures."}
```

### donut-chart

`<DonutChart>`, chart, category part-to-whole. Shows how 2 to 5 parts make up one whole, with each slice labelled by name and share.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Category field: one slice per distinct value.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field.
- `maxSlices`: `number`, default `5`. Most slices drawn, including "Other"; smaller categories are folded.
- `centerLabel`: `string`. Small label in the hole, e.g. "Total". Turns the centre text on.
- `centerValue`: `string | number`. Big text in the hole. Default: the formatted total when `centerLabel` is set.
- `otherLabel`: `string`, default `"Other"`. Name of the folded slice.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for category keys.

```json
{"type":"donut-chart","data":[{"tenure":"Own outright","households":8.8},{"tenure":"Own with a mortgage","households":7.4},{"tenure":"Rent privately","households":4.9},{"tenure":"Rent social housing","households":4.1}],"name":"tenure","value":"households","format":"{value}m","centerLabel":"households","highlight":"Rent privately","title":"4.9 million households in England rented privately in 2022-23","subtitle":"Households by tenure, England, 2022-23","source":"English Housing Survey","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### dumbbell-chart

`<DumbbellChart>`, chart, category comparison. Shows two values per category as dots joined by a line, so the length of the line shows the difference.

Props:

- `category` (required): `string`. Category field: one row of the chart each.
- `from` (required): `string`. Field with the first value, or (long data) the `series` value that marks it.
- `to` (required): `string`. Field with the second value, or (long data) the `series` value that marks it.
- `series`: `string`. Long data: the field whose values are `from` and `to`.
- `value`: `string`, default `"value"`. Long data: the measure field.
- `kind`: `"change" | "groups"`, default `"change"`. `change` draws a tint then the accent (before / after); `groups` uses two hues (two peers).
- `sort`: `"gap" | "from" | "to" | "none"`, default `"gap"`. Row order.
- `order`: `"desc" | "asc"`, default `"desc"`. Sort direction.
- `labels`: `boolean`. Value labels beside both dots. Default: on for up to 14 rows; otherwise a value axis is drawn.
- `gapLabel`: `boolean | string`, default `false`. Print the gap in a right-hand column; a string sets the column header.
- `zero`: `boolean`, default `false`. Start the value axis at zero.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for the `from` and `to` keys.

```json
{"type":"dumbbell-chart","data":[{"country":"South Korea","y2000":76,"y2023":83.6},{"country":"Turkey","y2000":71.1,"y2023":77.3},{"country":"Poland","y2000":73.8,"y2023":78.6},{"country":"Japan","y2000":81.2,"y2023":84.1},{"country":"Germany","y2000":78.2,"y2023":81.2},{"country":"United States","y2000":76.7,"y2023":78.4}],"category":"country","from":"y2000","to":"y2023","names":{"y2000":"2000","y2023":"2023"},"gapLabel":"Gain","format":"decimal:1","height":280,"title":"Life expectancy in South Korea rose from 76.0 years in 2000 to 83.6 in 2023","subtitle":"Life expectancy at birth, years, 2000 and 2023","source":"OECD Health Statistics (rounded)","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### fan-flow

`<FanFlow>`, chart, category poster. One solid block that splits into curved ribbons, each as thick as its value, ending at an aligned column of names, values and shares.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Destination field: one ribbon per distinct value.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: ribbon thickness. Rows sharing a name are summed; non-positive values are dropped.
- `trunk`: `string`. Label printed in the single block, with the total.
- `direction`: `"out" | "in"`, default `"out"`. `out`: one block fans out to many labels on the right. `in`: many labels on the left flow into one block.
- `maxItems`: `number`, default `12`. Ribbons to keep; the rest are summed into the remainder ribbon.
- `otherLabel`: `string`, default `"Other"`. Name of the remainder ribbon, drawn in the context colour. A row with this name is treated as the remainder.
- `tagged`: `string[]`. Destinations marked with a dotted outline around the name.
- `tagLabel`: `string`. What the dotted outline means, printed in the key. Needed for `tagged` to be drawn.
- `share`: `boolean`, default `true`. Print each ribbon's share of the total. Dropped on narrow screens.
- `colorBy`: `"series" | "none"`. `series`: one colour per destination; past the size of the theme's palette the extra colours are derived from the theme's own. `none`: every ribbon in the accent. Default: series while the destinations fit the palette (at most 8), none beyond.
- `sort`: `"value" | "none"`, default `"value"`. Largest first, or the data order.

```json
{"type":"fan-flow","data":[{"use":"Shower","litres":128},{"use":"Toilet","litres":97},{"use":"Washing machine","litres":62},{"use":"Kitchen tap","litres":45},{"use":"Dishwasher","litres":24},{"use":"Garden","litres":21},{"use":"Bathroom tap","litres":19},{"use":"Leaks","litres":16}],"name":"use","value":"litres","trunk":"Litres a day","tagged":["Shower","Washing machine","Dishwasher"],"tagLabel":"Uses heated water","title":"Showers used 128 of a household's 412 litres of water a day","subtitle":"Daily water use of one four-person household by use, litres","note":"Illustrative figures."}
```

### funnel-chart

`<FunnelChart>`, chart, category flow. Shows how many remain at each step of a sequence, with conversion and drop-off between steps.

Props:

- `stage` (required): `string`. Stage field. Rows are read in data order; the first row is the top of the funnel.
- `value` (required): `string`. Count field.
- `dropoff`: `boolean`, default `true`. State the drop-off between consecutive stages.
- `dropoffLabel`: `string`, default `"dropped off"`. Word for what is lost between stages.

```json
{"type":"funnel-chart","data":[{"step":"Visited the pricing page","users":48200},{"step":"Started a free trial","users":9640},{"step":"Connected a data source","users":5310},{"step":"Invited a teammate","users":2230},{"step":"Became a paying customer","users":1480}],"stage":"step","value":"users","format":"integer","title":"20% of pricing-page visitors started a free trial","subtitle":"Users reaching each step of the sign-up funnel, last 90 days","source":"Product analytics","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

### glyph-table

`<GlyphTable>`, HTML, category poster. A table with one row per entity in which every number is drawn as a small form chosen per column (counted dots, squares or icons, a ring, a sized circle, a bar) with the value printed beside it.

Props:

- `rows` (required): `Row[]`. One object per entity.
- `name`: `string`. Field holding the entity name. Defaults to the first key of the first row.
- `nameLabel`: `string`. Heading of the name column.
- `columns` (required): `{ field, label?, glyph?: "dots" | "blocks" | "ring" | "circle" | "bar" | "icons" | "text", unit?, format?, max?, icon? }[]`. Glyph columns in order. `dots`, `blocks` and `icons` draw one mark per `unit` (default 1, raised to a round number when the largest value would not fit, and stated in the heading). `ring` fills to `max` (default 100, or 1 for fractions). `circle` is sized by area and `bar` by length against `max` (default: the column's largest value). `text` prints the value alone.
- `order`: `string[]`. Entity names in display order; also assigns colours. Pass the same list to curve-rank to match its curve colours.
- `highlight`: `string | string[]`. Entities drawn in colour; every other row turns grey.
- `colorBy`: `"series" | "none"`. `series`: one colour per entity; past the size of the theme's palette the extra colours are derived from the theme's own (curve-rank derives the same ones). `none`: every row in the accent. Default: series while the rows fit the palette (at most 8), none beyond.
- `caption`: `string`. The table's title, as a real `<caption>`.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Measures, units and period, under the caption.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the table as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method notes or caveats, shown under the table.
- `select`: `boolean`. Let readers click a row (or press Enter on it) to select it; the other rows fade.
- `onSelect`: `(values: string[]) => void`. Called with the selected entity names whenever the selection changes.
- `selected`: `string[]`. Controlled selection: the entity names currently selected. When given, the table shows exactly this list and a click only calls `onSelect`. Omit it and the table keeps its own selection.

```json
{"type":"glyph-table","caption":"Filter coffee sold 310 cups a day at £2.40 a cup","subtitle":"Six drinks at one café: price, cups sold per day, share ordered with oat milk, seconds to prepare and caffeine","note":"Illustrative figures.","name":"drink","nameLabel":"Drink","columns":[{"field":"price","label":"Price per cup","glyph":"bar","format":{"style":"currency","currency":"GBP"},"max":5},{"field":"cups","label":"Cups sold a day","glyph":"dots","unit":10},{"field":"oat","label":"With oat milk","glyph":"ring","format":"{value}%"},{"field":"seconds","label":"Seconds to prepare","glyph":"blocks","unit":10},{"field":"caffeine","label":"Caffeine, mg","glyph":"circle"}],"rows":[{"drink":"Filter coffee","price":2.4,"cups":310,"oat":8,"seconds":15,"caffeine":140},{"drink":"Espresso","price":2.6,"cups":145,"oat":null,"seconds":30,"caffeine":65},{"drink":"Flat white","price":3.6,"cups":260,"oat":34,"seconds":95,"caffeine":130},{"drink":"Iced latte","price":4.2,"cups":180,"oat":41,"seconds":70,"caffeine":130},{"drink":"Matcha latte","price":4.8,"cups":75,"oat":57,"seconds":110,"caffeine":70},{"drink":"Hot chocolate","price":3.9,"cups":40,"oat":22,"seconds":85,"caffeine":10}]}
```

### headline

`<Headline>`, HTML, category text. The opening block of a piece or section: kicker, title, one-sentence deck and a byline/date line.

Props:

- `title` (required): `string`. One fact with its number, as a plain sentence. Wraps balanced.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: section, series or topic. Sentence case.
- `deck`: `string`. One-sentence standfirst.
- `byline`: `string`. Author line, shown as written, e.g. "By Ana Ruiz".
- `date`: `string`. ISO dates are formatted for the locale and wrapped in `<time>`; other strings are shown as written.
- `size`: `"page" | "section" | "card"`, default `"section"`. Type scale. Titles step down automatically in narrow containers.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`. Heading level. Defaults to 1 (page), 2 (section), 3 (card).
- `align`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Text alignment.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Extra content under the byline.

```json
{"type":"headline","size":"page","kicker":"Energy transition","title":"Solar generated more electricity than coal in Europe in 2024","deck":"Solar was the continent's second-largest source of electricity that year.","byline":"By Ana Ruiz and Tom Okafor","date":"2025-03-14"}
```

### heatmap

`<Heatmap>`, chart, category comparison. Colours a category-by-category (or time-by-category) grid by a numeric value, using a sequential or diverging scale.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. Column field: a category or a date.
- `y` (required): `string`. Row field.
- `value` (required): `string`. Numeric field that colours each cell. One data row per cell.
- `diverging`: `boolean`, default `false`. Diverging palette centred on `midpoint`, for values with a meaningful middle.
- `midpoint`: `number`, default `0`. Centre of the diverging scale.
- `labels`: `boolean`. Print the value in each cell. Default: on when cells are large enough.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Order rows by their total.
- `domain`: `[number, number]`. Fix the ends of the colour scale.

```json
{"type":"heatmap","data":[{"day":"Mon","slot":"6am","orders":12},{"day":"Mon","slot":"9am","orders":48},{"day":"Mon","slot":"12pm","orders":61},{"day":"Mon","slot":"3pm","orders":55},{"day":"Mon","slot":"6pm","orders":38},{"day":"Mon","slot":"9pm","orders":14},{"day":"Tue","slot":"6am","orders":11},{"day":"Tue","slot":"9am","orders":52}],"x":"slot","y":"day","value":"orders","title":"Orders peak at 70 per hour at 12pm on Wednesdays","subtitle":"Average orders per hour by weekday and time of day","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### histogram

`<Histogram>`, chart, category distribution. Bins a numeric field and shows how many rows fall in each bin, as touching bars on a continuous axis.

Props:

- `value` (required): `string`. Numeric field to bin.
- `bins`: `number`. Approximate number of bins; the width is rounded to a tidy step. Default: from the row count.
- `step`: `number`. Exact bin width in value units. Overrides `bins`.
- `median`: `boolean`, default `false`. Vertical marker at the median.
- `mean`: `boolean`, default `false`. Vertical marker at the mean.
- `normalize`: `boolean`, default `false`. Share of rows per bin instead of a count.
- `countLabel`: `string`. Title for the count axis, e.g. "Runners".

```json
{"type":"histogram","data":[{"minutes":14},{"minutes":18},{"minutes":18},{"minutes":19},{"minutes":20},{"minutes":21},{"minutes":21},{"minutes":22}],"value":"minutes","step":5,"median":true,"countLabel":"Commuters","format":"{value} min","title":"The median commute of 90 surveyed employees was 34.5 minutes","subtitle":"One-way commute time, in 5-minute bins","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### icon-array-grid

`<IconArrayGrid>`, chart, category poster. Compares many counts as a grid of labelled tiles, each holding an array of N icons with its name and number.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Category field: one tile per row.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: the count each tile shows.
- `unit`: `number`, default `1`. Units per icon.
- `unitLabel`: `string`. What one icon stands for, for the key line, e.g. "1 car".
- `total`: `number`. Draw every tile out of this many units, with uncounted icons as ghosts: 100 for a rate per 100.
- `icon`: `IconName | "path://..."`, default `"circle"`. Built-in icon name or a custom single SVG path.
- `perRow`: `number`, default `10`. Icons per line inside a tile.
- `columns`: `number`. Most tiles per line. Default: as many as fit at a readable size. Narrow containers use fewer.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Order of the tiles.

```json
{"type":"icon-array-grid","data":[{"district":"Ashby","cars":118},{"district":"Brook End","cars":104},{"district":"Castle Hill","cars":97},{"district":"Dockside","cars":41},{"district":"Eastfield","cars":88},{"district":"Fairmile","cars":126},{"district":"Greenway","cars":73},{"district":"Hollins","cars":110}],"name":"district","value":"cars","icon":"car","unitLabel":"1 car per 100 households","columns":4,"title":"Fairmile had 126 cars per 100 households in 2025","subtitle":"Cars per 100 households in 12 districts of Port Aldwin, 2025","source":"Illustrative data","note":"Invented figures for a fictional city"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### icon-stat

`<IconStat>`, HTML, category figure. A "1 in 4"-style statement: a row or grid of simple glyphs with some filled, and the sentence they illustrate.

Props:

- `count` (required): `number`. How many glyphs are filled.
- `total`: `number`, default `10`. How many glyphs are drawn. Capped at 100.
- `text`: `string`. The sentence completing the figure.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `text`.
- `value`: `string | false`. The figure as words. Defaults to "{count} in {total}"; `false` hides it.
- `icon`: `"circle" | "person" | "square" | IconName`, default `"circle"`. Glyph per unit. Filled units are solid, the rest outlined. Any other icon name from `core/icons.ts` also works; its unfilled units are faded instead of outlined.
- `columns`: `number`. Glyphs per row. Defaults to `total`, at most 10.
- `size`: `number`. Glyph height in px; shrinks to fit narrow containers.
- `tone`: `"accent" | "positive" | "negative" | "neutral"`, default `"accent"`. Fill colour by meaning.
- `align`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Alignment.

```json
{"type":"icon-stat","icon":"person","count":1,"total":4,"text":"households could not cover an unexpected bill of €500 without borrowing."}
```

### legend-key

`<LegendKey>`, HTML, category figure. A standalone colour key: categorical swatches, or a sequential/diverging ramp with end labels.

Props:

- `scale`: `"categorical" | "sequential" | "diverging"`. Defaults to `categorical` when `items` is given, otherwise `sequential`.
- `items`: `(string | { label, color?, index?, shape?, muted? })[]`. Categorical entries. Colours come from the theme's categorical order by position (or `index`) unless given.
- `labels`: `string[]`. Ramp end labels: `[low, high]` or `[low, middle, high]`.
- `colors`: `string[]`. Ramp colours, low to high. Defaults to the theme's sequential or diverging ramp.
- `stepped`: `boolean`, default `false`. Discrete steps instead of a continuous gradient, for binned scales.
- `title`: `string`. What the key encodes.
- `shape`: `"square" | "line" | "dot"`, default `"square"`. Default swatch shape: match the marks.
- `orientation`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `"horizontal"`. Categorical layout.
- `width`: `number`, default `240`. Ramp width in px, capped at the container.
- `align`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Alignment within the container.

```json
{"type":"legend-key","title":"Source of electricity","items":["Solar","Wind","Hydro","Gas",{"label":"Other","muted":true}]}
```

### line-chart

`<LineChart>`, chart, category trend. Shows how one or more values change over time or another ordered dimension.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. Time or ordered category field. ISO dates are placed on a true time axis.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. Value field, or several (one line each).
- `series`: `string`. Field that splits rows into lines (long data).
- `curve`: `"linear" | "smooth" | "step"`, default `"linear"`. Line shape.
- `area`: `boolean`, default `false`. Light fill under the line; forces a zero baseline.
- `endLabels`: `boolean`. Name each line at its end. Default: on for up to 6 lines.
- `points`: `boolean`. Marker on every point. Default: on for 12 points or fewer.
- `zero`: `boolean`, default `false`. Start the value axis at zero.
- `log`: `boolean`, default `false`. Logarithmic value axis.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for series keys.
- `contextLabels`: `boolean | string`, default `false`. With `highlight`: name the grey context lines. `true` adds a muted end label to each when they all fit; a string such as `"Other cities"` adds one muted legend entry instead. On narrow charts the legend already lists every line.

```json
{"type":"line-chart","data":[{"year":"2019","solar":2.7,"wind":5.3},{"year":"2020","solar":3.2,"wind":5.9},{"year":"2021","solar":3.7,"wind":6.5},{"year":"2022","solar":4.6,"wind":7.3},{"year":"2023","solar":5.5,"wind":7.8}],"x":"year","y":["solar","wind"],"format":"{value}%","title":"Solar's share rose from 2.7% to 5.5% between 2019 and 2023"}
```

### lollipop-chart

`<LollipopChart>`, chart, category comparison. Ranks categories with a dot on a thin stem from zero, or as a stemless dot plot on a free scale.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. Category field.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. Value field. Several fields draw several dots per row (dot plot).
- `series`: `string`. Field that splits rows into series (long data). Forces the dot plot.
- `stem`: `boolean`, default `true`. Stem from zero. `false` draws a dot plot whose scale need not start at zero.
- `orientation`: `"auto" | "horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `"auto"`. Horizontal for rankings, vertical for dates.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`. Row order. Default: descending for rankings, data order for dates.
- `labels`: `boolean`. Value beside each dot. Default: on for one series of up to 16 rows.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for series keys.

```json
{"type":"lollipop-chart","data":[{"country":"Netherlands","share":27},{"country":"Denmark","share":19},{"country":"Germany","share":10},{"country":"Sweden","share":9},{"country":"Japan","share":8},{"country":"France","share":4},{"country":"United Kingdom","share":2},{"country":"United States","share":1}],"x":"country","y":"share","format":"{value}%","height":300,"title":"27% of trips in the Netherlands are made by bike","subtitle":"Share of all trips made by bicycle","source":"National travel surveys, latest available year (rounded)","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### nested-shares

`<NestedShares>`, chart, category poster. Shows several shares of the same whole, such as one share at five dates, as outlines nested from one corner of a square, each enclosing an area equal to its share.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Field naming each share: a period ("2025") or a category.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: each row's share of the whole.
- `total`: `number`. The whole. Default: 1 when every value is at most 1, otherwise 100.
- `wholeLabel`: `string`. What the outer square stands for, printed under it, e.g. "All trips".
- `corner`: `"bottom-left" | "top-left"`, default `"bottom-left"`. The corner every outline grows from.

```json
{"type":"nested-shares","data":[{"year":"2005","share":4},{"year":"2010","share":7},{"year":"2015","share":12},{"year":"2020","share":19},{"year":"2025","share":27}],"name":"year","value":"share","format":"{value}%","highlight":"2025","wholeLabel":"All trips in the city","title":"Bicycles made 27% of trips in Port Aldwin in 2025","subtitle":"Share of all trips made by bicycle, 2005 to 2025","source":"Illustrative data","note":"Invented figures for a fictional city"}
```

### orbit-chart

`<OrbitChart>`, chart, category poster. Places items as dots on concentric rings round a centre, one ring per category, level or period, with a key that explains rings, angle and dot area.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Name field: one dot per row.
- `ring` (required): `string`. Field naming the ring each dot sits on: a category, level or period.
- `rings`: `string[]`. Ring order from the centre outward. Default: first appearance in the data.
- `value`: `string`. Value field: dot area. Without it every dot is the same size.
- `angle`: `string`. Numeric field that sets the angle round the ring. Without it dots are spaced evenly.
- `angleDomain`: `[number, number]`, default `[0, 360]`. Values of `angle` that map to a full turn, clockwise from 12 o'clock.
- `ringLabel`: `string`. What the rings mean, for the key. Default: the `ring` field name.
- `angleLabel`: `string`. What the angle means, for the key, e.g. "Clockwise from the top: month of launch".
- `sizeLabel`: `string`. What dot area means, for the key. Default: the `value` field name.
- `icon`: `string`. Icon in the centre disc: a built-in name or `path://`.
- `centerLabel`: `string`. Short text in the centre disc, used when there is no `icon`.
- `colorBy`: `"ring" | "single"`, default `"ring"`. A colour per ring, or the accent for every dot.
- `showKey`: `boolean`, default `true`. Show the key that explains rings, angle and dot area.

```json
{"type":"orbit-chart","data":[{"supplier":"Halden Cells","tier":"Tier 1","spend":84},{"supplier":"Orrin Motors","tier":"Tier 1","spend":61},{"supplier":"Vale Castings","tier":"Tier 1","spend":37},{"supplier":"Kestrel Wiring","tier":"Tier 2","spend":22},{"supplier":"Brask Cathodes","tier":"Tier 2","spend":48},{"supplier":"Lumen Glass","tier":"Tier 2","spend":15},{"supplier":"Pell Magnets","tier":"Tier 2","spend":29},{"supplier":"Tarn Lithium","tier":"Tier 3","spend":33}],"name":"supplier","ring":"tier","value":"spend","format":"${value}m","centerLabel":"Car plant","highlight":"Brask Cathodes","ringLabel":"Tier 1 sells to the plant, each further ring sells to the ring inside it","sizeLabel":"annual spend","title":"Brask Cathodes is a tier 2 supplier with $48 million of annual spend","subtitle":"12 suppliers to one car plant by supply-chain tier, annual spend in $ million","note":"Illustrative figures for invented companies"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### pictogram-chart

`<PictogramChart>`, chart, category comparison. Compares quantities with rows of repeated icons, each icon standing for a fixed number of units.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Category field: one row of icons per category.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field.
- `unit`: `number`. Units per icon. Default: a round number giving the largest row about ten icons.
- `unitLabel`: `string`. What one icon stands for, for the key line, e.g. "1 million people".
- `icon`: `IconName | "path://..."`, default `"person"`. Built-in icon name from `core/icons.ts` ("person", "house", "car", "tree", "coin", "drop", "bolt", "wind-turbine", "wheat" and about 60 more) or a custom single SVG path.
- `icons`: `Record<string, string>`. Icon per category key; falls back to `icon`.
- `perRow`: `number`. Wrap rows after this many icons. Default: as many as fit.
- `labels`: `boolean`, default `true`. Print the value after each row.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Row order.

```json
{"type":"pictogram-chart","data":[{"city":"Tokyo","people":37.1},{"city":"Delhi","people":33.8},{"city":"Shanghai","people":29.9},{"city":"São Paulo","people":22.8},{"city":"Mexico City","people":22.5}],"name":"city","value":"people","unit":2,"unitLabel":"2 million people","format":"{value}m","highlight":"Delhi","title":"Delhi had 33.8 million people in 2024, 3.3 million fewer than Tokyo","subtitle":"Population of the five largest urban agglomerations, 2024","source":"UN World Urbanization Prospects","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### pill-rank

`<PillRank>`, chart, category poster. Shows a ranked list as horizontally centred rounded bars, with each name in capitals on its pill, the value at the left edge and the rank at the right.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Name field: one row per data row.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: pill width. Non-positive values are dropped.
- `sort`: `boolean`, default `true`. Sort rows largest first. Set false to keep the data order.
- `compare`: `string[]`. Names of rows that are not ranked: drawn below a dotted rule, without a rank number.
- `compareLabel`: `string`. Short heading over the comparison rows, e.g. "For comparison".
- `max`: `number`. Value that fills the full pill width. Default: the largest value.
- `ranks`: `boolean`, default `true`. Show the rank number at the right edge.

```json
{"type":"pill-rank","data":[{"river":"Nile","km":6650},{"river":"Amazon","km":6400},{"river":"Yangtze","km":6300},{"river":"Mississippi-Missouri","km":6275},{"river":"Yenisei","km":5539},{"river":"Yellow River","km":5464},{"river":"Ob-Irtysh","km":5410},{"river":"Congo","km":4700}],"name":"river","value":"km","format":"{value} km","highlight":"Congo","compare":["Danube","Rhine"],"compareLabel":"Europe, for comparison","title":"The Congo is 4,700 km long","subtitle":"Length of eight major river systems and two European rivers, kilometres","source":"Encyclopaedia Britannica","note":"Lengths of river systems are approximate and vary by source"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### progress-meter

`<ProgressMeter>`, HTML, category figure. A labelled horizontal meter of one value against a maximum or target, with the target marked and the value printed.

Props:

- `value` (required): `number`. The current value.
- `label` (required): `string`. What is measured, sentence case.
- `max`: `number`. End of the track. Defaults to the target, or 1 with no target.
- `min`: `number`, default `0`. Start of the track.
- `target`: `number`. A goal or threshold, drawn as a tick and labelled.
- `targetLabel`: `string`, default `"Target"`. Name for the target tick.
- `showMax`: `boolean`. Print "of {max}" after the value. Default: only when `max` is given.
- `context`: `string`. A line under the meter that gives the number meaning.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`. Number format. Defaults to `"percent"` when the track ends at 1 or less, otherwise `"auto"`.
- `tone`: `"accent" | "positive" | "negative" | "neutral"`, default `"accent"`. Fill colour by meaning.
- `size`: `"sm" | "md"`, default `"md"`. `sm` for dense stacks.

```json
{"type":"progress-meter","label":"Homes with a heat pump or district heating","value":0.46,"max":1,"showMax":false,"target":0.7,"targetLabel":"2030 target","context":"Up from 31% in 2020. At the current rate the target is reached in 2033."}
```

### proportional-area

`<ProportionalArea>`, chart, category poster. Compares two to eight values as squares or circles whose areas are proportional to the values, each printed with its name and number.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Category field: one shape per row.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field. Each shape's area is proportional to it.
- `shape`: `"square" | "circle"`, default `"square"`. Squares or circles.
- `layout`: `"row" | "nested" | "packed"`, default `"row"`. `row`: side by side on a common baseline. `nested`: inside one another from a shared corner (squares) or lowest point (circles). `packed`: clustered together.
- `ratio`: `boolean | string`. Print how many times the largest value is the smallest. `true` for "{largest} is {ratio} times {smallest}", or a template with those placeholders.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Order of the shapes in the row layout. Nested and packed always draw largest first.

```json
{"type":"proportional-area","data":[{"lake":"Superior","area":82100},{"lake":"Victoria","area":68900},{"lake":"Tanganyika","area":32900},{"lake":"Erie","area":25700},{"lake":"Titicaca","area":8370}],"name":"lake","value":"area","format":"integer","ratio":true,"title":"Lake Superior covers 82,100 km², 9.8 times Lake Titicaca","subtitle":"Surface area of five lakes, square kilometres","source":"Approximate published figures","note":"Rounded, for illustration"}
```

### prose

`<Prose>`, HTML, category text. A readable block of narration at a 45-75 character measure, for the text between charts.

Props:

- `text`: `string | string[]`. Narration. Blank lines separate paragraphs. Supports `**bold**`, `*italic*` and `[link](url)`.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `text`.
- `size`: `"sm" | "md" | "lg"`, default `"md"`. Body size: 14, 16 or 18px.
- `measure`: `number`, default `65`. Line length in characters, clamped to 45-75.
- `lead`: `boolean`, default `false`. Set the first paragraph a step larger.
- `tone`: `"default" | "muted"`, default `"default"`. `muted` for secondary narration.
- `align`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Centres the block (text stays left-aligned).

```json
{"type":"prose","text":"In 2015 solar supplied **3% of Europe's electricity**. Hydro supplied more than three times as much.\n\nPanel prices fell by about 80% in the years that followed. In 2024 solar generated more electricity than coal across the EU, according to [Ember's annual review](https://ember-energy.org).\n\nSolar's share differs by country. The next chart shows it for each EU member state."}
```

### pull-quote

`<PullQuote>`, HTML, category text. A large quotation with its attribution.

Props:

- `quote`: `string`. The words quoted, without quotation marks.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `quote`.
- `attribution`: `string`. Who said it.
- `role`: `string`. Their role, or where it was said.
- `cite`: `string`. Source URL: set as the blockquote `cite` and linked from the attribution.
- `size`: `"md" | "lg"`, default `"lg"`. `lg` anchors a section; `md` sits inside a column.
- `align`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Left-aligned quotes carry a side rule; centred ones do not.

```json
{"type":"pull-quote","quote":"Solar set the midday wholesale price on most days in 2023. Our plans had assumed that would happen in the 2030s.","attribution":"Marit de Vries","role":"Head of system operations, Dutch grid operator"}
```

### radial-bar-chart

`<RadialBarChart>`, chart, category trend. Draws bars around a circle for data that repeats in a cycle, such as hours of the day or months of the year.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. The cyclical category field, in cycle order.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. Value field, or several to stack.
- `series`: `string`. Field that splits rows into stacked series (long data).
- `labelEvery`: `number`. Label every nth category around the rim. Default: chosen to avoid crowding.
- `labels`: `boolean`. Print the value on the tallest bar. Default: on for a single series.
- `centerFirst`: `boolean`, default `false`. Centre the first category on 12 o'clock (compass directions) instead of starting its band there (hours).
- `centerLabel`: `string`. Text in the centre of the ring, e.g. "24 hours".
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for series keys.

```json
{"type":"radial-bar-chart","data":[{"hour":"00:00","trips":2.1},{"hour":"01:00","trips":1.2},{"hour":"02:00","trips":0.8},{"hour":"03:00","trips":0.6},{"hour":"04:00","trips":0.7},{"hour":"05:00","trips":1.4},{"hour":"06:00","trips":3.6},{"hour":"07:00","trips":6.9}],"x":"hour","y":"trips","format":"{value}%","centerLabel":"24 hours","highlight":["08:00","17:00"],"title":"Weekday bike-share trips peak at 9.2% in the 5pm hour and 8.8% in the 8am hour","subtitle":"Share of daily bike-share trips starting in each hour, weekdays","source":"Illustrative bike-share data"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### radial-spokes

`<RadialSpokes>`, chart, category poster. Draws one spoke per row radiating from a centre disc, each as long as its value, with the name and value set on an outer ring.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Name field: one spoke per row, in data order, clockwise.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: spoke length from the centre disc.
- `shape`: `"bar" | "line"`, default `"bar"`. A thick tapered bar with a round head, or a thin line ending in a dot.
- `icon`: `string`. Icon in the centre disc: a built-in name or `path://`.
- `centerLabel`: `string`. Short text in the centre disc, used when there is no `icon`.
- `ring`: `boolean`, default `true`. Dotted outer ring at the scale maximum, where the labels sit.
- `max`: `number`. Value that reaches the outer ring. Default: the largest value.
- `startAngle`: `number`, default `0`. Angle of the first spoke in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock.
- `sweep`: `number`, default `360`. Arc the spokes are spread over, in degrees. 180 makes a fan.
- `colorBy`: `"single" | "value"`, default `"single"`. The accent for every spoke, or a shade by value along the sequential ramp.

```json
{"type":"radial-spokes","data":[{"use":"Space heating","share":42},{"use":"Hot water","share":17},{"use":"Cooking","share":6},{"use":"Fridge and freezer","share":8},{"use":"Laundry","share":7},{"use":"Lighting","share":5},{"use":"Screens and computers","share":9},{"use":"Everything else","share":6}],"name":"use","value":"share","format":"{value}%","icon":"house","highlight":"Space heating","title":"Space heating uses 42% of a home's energy","subtitle":"Share of household energy by end use, a typical home in a cool climate","note":"Illustrative figures"}
```

### ribbon-chart

`<RibbonChart>`, chart, category poster. One filled band per entity across periods: its thickness is its value in each period and its vertical position is its rank, so bands cross as the order changes.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. Period field: one column of the ribbon per distinct value, in data order.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. Value field (long data), or one column per entity (wide data). Band thickness; negative values are drawn as zero.
- `series`: `string`. Entity field, for long data.
- `values`: `boolean`, default `true`. Print each value inside its band at every period where it fits.
- `labels`: `"both" | "end"`. Entity names at both ends, or only at the end. Default: both, end only on narrow screens.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for entity keys.
- `colorBy`: `"auto" | "series" | "none"`, default `"auto"`. `auto`: the largest entities take the theme's colours and any past the palette size (at most 8) are grey. `series`: every band gets its own colour, the extra ones derived from the theme's own. `none`: every band in the accent.

```json
{"type":"ribbon-chart","data":[{"year":"2019","Potatoes":7.4,"Carrots":5.1,"Onions":4.2,"Beans":2.6,"Squash":1.2},{"year":"2020","Potatoes":6.9,"Carrots":5.6,"Onions":3.8,"Beans":3.1,"Squash":2.3},{"year":"2021","Potatoes":6.1,"Carrots":5.9,"Onions":3.1,"Beans":3.4,"Squash":3.9},{"year":"2022","Potatoes":5.2,"Carrots":6.3,"Onions":2.9,"Beans":3.2,"Squash":5},{"year":"2023","Potatoes":4.8,"Carrots":6,"Onions":2.4,"Beans":3.6,"Squash":6.1},{"year":"2024","Potatoes":4.1,"Carrots":6.2,"Onions":2.2,"Beans":3.5,"Squash":6.8}],"x":"year","y":["Potatoes","Carrots","Onions","Beans","Squash"],"format":"{value} t","title":"The squash harvest rose from 1.2 to 6.8 tonnes between 2019 and 2024","subtitle":"Harvest of five crops at one community farm, tonnes, 2019 to 2024, largest at the top each year","note":"Illustrative figures."}
```

### sankey-chart

`<SankeyChart>`, chart, category flow. Shows how a quantity flows from sources through stages to destinations, with link width proportional to the flow.

Props:

- `from`: `string`, default `"source"`. Field naming where each flow starts. Not called `source` because that is the figure's source line.
- `to`: `string`, default `"target"`. Field naming where each flow ends.
- `value`: `string`, default `"value"`. Flow size field. Non-positive flows are dropped.
- `orientation`: `"auto" | "horizontal" | "vertical"`, default `"auto"`. Left to right, or top to bottom for narrow columns with short names.
- `labels`: `boolean`, default `true`. Print each node's total after its name.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for node keys.

```json
{"type":"sankey-chart","data":[{"from":"Coal","to":"Electricity","twh":290},{"from":"Gas","to":"Electricity","twh":210},{"from":"Gas","to":"Heat","twh":330},{"from":"Wind and solar","to":"Electricity","twh":240},{"from":"Nuclear","to":"Electricity","twh":120},{"from":"Oil","to":"Transport","twh":560},{"from":"Oil","to":"Heat","twh":90},{"from":"Electricity","to":"Homes","twh":280}],"from":"from","to":"to","value":"twh","format":"{value} TWh","title":"220 TWh of the 860 TWh used to generate electricity was lost","subtitle":"Energy flows from fuel to end use, terawatt-hours per year","source":"Illustrative national energy balance"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### scale-ladder

`<ScaleLadder>`, chart, category poster. A tall vertical band graded along one scale (linear or log, running up or down) with each item placed at its true position and labelled with an icon, its name and its value on alternating sides.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Field holding each item's name.
- `value` (required): `string`. Field holding each item's position on the scale.
- `icon`: `IconInput`. One icon for every item: a built-in name or a `path://` string. Items without an icon get a dot.
- `iconField`: `string`. Field holding a per-item icon name or `path://` string. Overrides `icon`.
- `scale`: `"linear" | "log"`, default `"linear"`. Log spaces the scale by powers of ten; the heading over the band says so.
- `direction`: `"up" | "down"`, default `"up"`. `up`: larger values higher (height, temperature). `down`: larger values lower (depth, age).
- `min`: `number`. Start of the scale. Default: a round number at or below the smallest value.
- `max`: `number`. End of the scale. Default: a round number at or above the largest value.
- `ticks`: `number[]`. Values that get a boxed label on the band. Default: round steps, or powers of ten on a log scale.
- `zones`: `{ from: number; to: number; label: string }[]`. Named ranges along the scale, shaded across the graphic and named along its outer edge.
- `scaleLabel`: `string`. Heading over the band: the measure and its unit, e.g. "Depth, metres".
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for item keys.
- `bandWidth`: `number`. Width of the band in px, at most 40% of the plot width. Default 60, or 46 on narrow screens.

```json
{"type":"scale-ladder","data":[{"thing":"Fridge","c":4},{"thing":"Chocolate melts","c":34},{"thing":"Egg white sets","c":62},{"thing":"Water boils","c":100,"icon":"drop"},{"thing":"Sugar caramelises","c":170},{"thing":"Deep-frying oil","c":180,"icon":"drop"},{"thing":"Bread bakes","c":220},{"thing":"Home oven at full heat","c":250}],"name":"thing","value":"c","iconField":"icon","format":"{value}°C","scaleLabel":"Temperature","min":0,"max":500,"zones":[{"from":0,"to":100,"label":"Below boiling"},{"from":100,"to":250,"label":"Home oven range"},{"from":250,"to":500,"label":"Wood-fired oven range"}],"title":"Nine kitchen temperatures from 4°C to 450°C","subtitle":"Typical temperatures in a kitchen, degrees Celsius","note":"Approximate, rounded figures."}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### scatter-chart

`<ScatterChart>`, chart, category relationship. Plots two numeric measures against each other, one dot per row, with optional bubble size, group colour, selective labels and a trend line.

Props:

- `x` (required): `string`. Numeric field on the horizontal axis.
- `y` (required): `string`. Numeric field on the vertical axis.
- `size`: `string`. Numeric field for bubble size; area is proportional to the value.
- `series`: `string`. Field that colours points by group. Beyond 4 groups the smallest fold into a grey Other.
- `label`: `string`. Field naming each point, for tooltips, direct labels and `highlight`.
- `labels`: `"auto" | "all" | "none" | string[]`, default `"auto"`. Which points are labelled. `auto`: highlighted points, or the outliers when nothing is highlighted. Overlapping labels are hidden.
- `trend`: `boolean`, default `false`. Least-squares line of best fit through all points.
- `logX`: `boolean`, default `false`. Logarithmic x axis.
- `logY`: `boolean`, default `false`. Logarithmic y axis.
- `xLabel`: `string`. x axis title. Defaults to the field name.
- `yLabel`: `string`. y axis title. Defaults to the field name.
- `xFormat`: `FormatSpec`. Format for x values; `format` applies to y.
- `opacity`: `number`. Point opacity. Default falls as the point count rises.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for series keys.

```json
{"type":"scatter-chart","data":[{"country":"United States","spend":12555,"life":77.5},{"country":"Switzerland","spend":8049,"life":83.9},{"country":"Germany","spend":8011,"life":80.8},{"country":"Norway","spend":7771,"life":83.2},{"country":"Netherlands","spend":6729,"life":81.4},{"country":"France","spend":6630,"life":82.4},{"country":"Canada","spend":6319,"life":81.6},{"country":"Sweden","spend":6438,"life":83.1}],"x":"spend","y":"life","label":"country","highlight":"United States","labels":["United States","Japan","Mexico","Switzerland","Poland"],"xFormat":"currency:USD","xLabel":"Health spending per person","yLabel":"Life expectancy, years","title":"The United States spent $12,555 per person on health in 2022","subtitle":"Health spending per person (US$, PPP) against life expectancy at birth, OECD countries, 2022. US life expectancy was 77.5 years.","source":"OECD Health Statistics (rounded)","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### segmented-bar

`<SegmentedBar>`, chart, category part-to-whole. Splits one whole into proportional segments along a single horizontal bar.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Category field: one segment per distinct value.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field.
- `size`: `"tall" | "thin"`, default `"tall"`. 28px with shares printed inside where they fit, or 8px unlabelled.
- `sort`: `"none" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Segment order; the legend follows it.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for category keys.

```json
{"type":"segmented-bar","data":[{"party":"Labour","seats":411},{"party":"Conservative","seats":121},{"party":"Liberal Democrat","seats":72},{"party":"SNP","seats":9},{"party":"Others","seats":37}],"name":"party","value":"seats","title":"Labour won 411 of 650 seats in the 2024 general election","subtitle":"Seats in the House of Commons by party after the 2024 general election","source":"House of Commons Library","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### shape-fill

`<ShapeFill>`, chart, category poster. Shows one or more percentages as icon silhouettes filled from the bottom to that level, with the number printed large beside each.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Label field: one silhouette per row.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: how full each silhouette is, against `max`.
- `max`: `number`. The value that fills a silhouette completely. Default: 1 when every value is at most 1, otherwise 100.
- `icon`: `IconName | "path://..."`, default `"drop"`. Built-in icon name or a custom single SVG path.
- `icons`: `Record<string, string>`. Icon per label; falls back to `icon`.
- `columns`: `number`. Silhouettes per line. Default: up to four, two on a phone.
- `colorBy`: `"single" | "item"`, default `"single"`. `single`: every silhouette in the accent colour. `item`: one colour per row.
- `iconSize`: `number`. Silhouette height in px. Default: sized to the width, or grown to fill the box when the `height` prop or `aspect` is given, so one silhouette can be the main figure of a poster.

```json
{"type":"shape-fill","data":[{"reservoir":"Carrow","level":63},{"reservoir":"Upper Fen","level":41},{"reservoir":"Stonebeck","level":88}],"name":"reservoir","value":"level","icon":"drop","format":"{value}%","title":"Carrow Reservoir was 63% full on 1 September 2025","subtitle":"Water stored as a share of capacity, three reservoirs, 1 September 2025","source":"Illustrative data","note":"Invented figures for fictional reservoirs"}
```

### slope-chart

`<SlopeChart>`, chart, category trend. Connects each entity's value at two (or a few) points with a straight line, labelled with name and value at both ends.

Props:

- `series` (required): `string`. Entity field: one line each.
- `x`: `string`. Period field for long data. Omit when each row is an entity with one column per period.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. Value field (long data), or the period columns in order (one row per entity).
- `colorBy`: `"none" | "direction" | "series"`, default `"none"`. Accent for all lines, positive / negative by direction, or one hue per entity (up to 8).
- `good`: `"up" | "down"`, default `"up"`. Direction that takes the positive colour when colouring by direction.
- `labels`: `"both" | "end"`. Entity names at both ends or only the end. Default: both; end only on narrow screens.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for entity keys and period columns.

```json
{"type":"slope-chart","data":[{"country":"United Kingdom","y2012":39,"y2023":1},{"country":"Germany","y2012":44,"y2023":26},{"country":"United States","y2012":37,"y2023":16},{"country":"Poland","y2012":84,"y2023":61},{"country":"India","y2012":71,"y2023":75},{"country":"Japan","y2012":29,"y2023":32}],"series":"country","y":["y2012","y2023"],"names":{"y2012":"2012","y2023":"2023"},"highlight":"United Kingdom","format":"{value}%","title":"The UK's coal share of electricity fell from 39% to 1% between 2012 and 2023","subtitle":"Share of electricity generated from coal, 2012 and 2023","source":"Ember (rounded)","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### small-multiples

`<SmallMultiples>`, chart, category trend. Repeats one small line, area or bar chart per value of a facet field on a shared scale, each panel titled.

Props:

- `facet` (required): `string`. Field whose values each get a panel.
- `x` (required): `string`. Time or ordered category field, shared by every panel.
- `y` (required): `string | string[]`. Value field, or several (one series each in every panel).
- `series`: `string`. Field that splits rows into series inside each panel (long data).
- `kind`: `"line" | "area" | "bar"`, default `"line"`. What each panel draws. Area and bar panels start at zero.
- `columns`: `number`. Preferred number of columns; reduced automatically on narrow containers.
- `scales`: `"shared" | "free"`, default `"shared"`. Shared value scale across panels, or each panel on its own (say so in the subtitle).
- `context`: `boolean`, default `false`. Draw every other panel's line faintly behind each panel's own.
- `latest`: `boolean`. Print the latest value beside each panel title. Default: on for a single series.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for facet values and series keys.

```json
{"type":"small-multiples","data":[{"country":"Germany","year":"2010","rate":6.8},{"country":"Germany","year":"2013","rate":5},{"country":"Germany","year":"2015","rate":4.6},{"country":"Germany","year":"2017","rate":3.8},{"country":"Germany","year":"2019","rate":3.1},{"country":"Germany","year":"2021","rate":3.6},{"country":"Germany","year":"2023","rate":3},{"country":"Germany","year":"2024","rate":3.4}],"facet":"country","x":"year","y":"rate","highlight":"Greece","format":"{value}%","title":"Greek unemployment fell from 27.5% in 2013 to 10.1% in 2024","subtitle":"Unemployment rate, 2010 to 2024, same scale in every panel","source":"Eurostat (rounded)","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### source-note

`<SourceNote>`, HTML, category text. A sourcing footer for a whole piece: sources with optional links, the period covered, method, caveats and credit.

Props:

- `sources`: `string | { name, url? } | (string | { name, url? })[]`. Where the data comes from. Entries with a `url` are linked.
- `period`: `string`. The period the data covers, e.g. "2015 to 2024". Shown as "Data".
- `method`: `string`. How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions.
- `note`: `string`. Caveats the reader should know.
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the piece.
- `layout`: `"list" | "inline"`, default `"list"`. Labelled list, or one running paragraph.
- `rule`: `boolean`, default `true`. Hairline above the note.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Extra content after the rows.

```json
{"type":"source-note","sources":[{"name":"Ember, European Electricity Review 2025","url":"https://ember-energy.org"},{"name":"ENTSO-E Transparency Platform","url":"https://transparency.entsoe.eu"}],"note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration","period":"January 2015 to December 2024, monthly","method":"Generation shares are net of pumped-storage consumption. Figures for 2024 are provisional and exclude Malta and Cyprus.","credit":"Analysis and charts by the data desk"}
```

### sparkline

`<Sparkline>`, chart, category trend. A word-sized line or bar series without axes, with the latest point marked.

Props:

- `y` (required): `string`. Value field.
- `x`: `string`. Time or label field, used in the tooltip and alt text. Rows are drawn in data order.
- `mark`: `"line" | "bar"`, default `"line"`. Line for a trend, bars for discrete counts or gains and losses (negative bars take the negative colour).
- `extremes`: `boolean`, default `false`. Mark the lowest and highest points with small dots.
- `band`: `[number, number]`. Shaded reference range in value units, e.g. a normal range.
- `area`: `boolean`, default `false`. Light fill under the line; forces a zero baseline.
- `showValue`: `boolean`, default `false`. Print the last value after the line.
- `zero`: `boolean`. Include zero in the scale. Default: off for lines, always on for bars.

```json
{"type":"sparkline","data":[{"month":"2023-07","rate":3.9},{"month":"2023-08","rate":3.8},{"month":"2023-09","rate":3.8},{"month":"2023-10","rate":3.6},{"month":"2023-11","rate":3.5},{"month":"2023-12","rate":3.6},{"month":"2024-01","rate":3.4},{"month":"2024-02","rate":3.7}],"x":"month","y":"rate","format":"{value}%","showValue":true,"extremes":true,"style":{"maxWidth":220},"alt":"Sparkline of the unemployment rate over 16 months, July 2023 to October 2024. It started at 3.9%, fell to 3.4% in January 2024 and ended at 4.4%, the highest in the period."}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### stat-circles

`<StatCircles>`, chart, category poster. Shows a few related magnitudes as plain circles sized by area, each with its number set large and a short label.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Label field: the short text under or beside each circle.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: circle area, and the number printed large. Non-positive values are dropped.
- `unit`: `string`. Unit printed small after each number, e.g. "kg". Leave out when `format` already includes it.
- `layout`: `"row" | "steps" | "nested"`, default `"row"`. Circles centred on one line, standing on a shared baseline, or drawn inside each other from a shared lowest point. Narrow containers stack a row or steps into a column.
- `colorBy`: `"item" | "value" | "single"`, default `"item"`. A colour per circle, a shade by value along the sequential ramp, or the accent for all.
- `icon`: `string | Record<string, string>`. Icon above the number in large circles: one for all, or a map from label to icon. Built-in name or `path://`.

```json
{"type":"stat-circles","data":[{"who":"per person in the United States","kg":124},{"who":"per person in Brazil","kg":100},{"who":"per person in China","kg":63},{"who":"per person in India","kg":6}],"name":"who","value":"kg","unit":"kg","title":"Meat supply in the United States was 124 kg per person in 2021","subtitle":"Meat supply per person per year, kilograms, 2021","source":"FAO food balance sheets","note":"Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"}
```

### stat-tile

`<StatTile>`, HTML, category figure. A compact, bordered KPI tile: label, value, change against a baseline and an optional trend graphic.

Props:

- `label` (required): `string`. What it measures, sentence case.
- `value` (required): `number | string`. The figure. Numbers are formatted with `format`.
- `delta`: `number | string`. Change against a baseline. Numbers render as signed percentages (0.12 is +12%).
- `deltaLabel`: `string`. What the delta is against, e.g. "vs last month".
- `upIsGood`: `boolean`, default `true`. Whether an increase is an improvement. Sets the delta colour.
- `context`: `string`. A line that states a comparison or reference for the number.
- `trend`: `Slot | number[]`. A chart spec, a React element, or an array of numbers drawn as a sparkline.
- `trendPosition`: `"bottom" | "right"`, default `"bottom"`. Where the trend sits; `right` falls back to `bottom` under 280px.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"auto"`. Number format for `value`.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Extra content at the bottom of the tile.

```json
{"type":"stat-tile","label":"Monthly active users","value":48210,"format":"compact","delta":0.083,"deltaLabel":"vs September","trend":[38.1,39.4,39,40.8,42.2,41.9,43.5,44.1,44.5,46,47.2,48.2],"style":{"maxWidth":300}}
```

### step-marker

`<StepMarker>`, HTML, category text. A numbered chapter or step heading ("01 — Electricity sources in 2015") for sequencing the sections of a story.

Props:

- `step` (required): `number | string`. Step number, zero-padded to two digits. Strings are shown as written.
- `title` (required): `string`. The chapter or step title.
- `total`: `number`. Total steps; the marker then reads "02 / 05".
- `text`: `string`. A sentence under the title.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `text`.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `2`. Heading level.
- `size`: `"md" | "lg"`, default `"md"`. `lg` for chapter openers.
- `layout`: `"inline" | "stacked"`, default `"inline"`. Number beside or above the title. Narrow containers always stack.
- `rule`: `boolean`, default `false`. Hairline above the marker.

```json
{"type":"step-marker","step":1,"title":"Electricity sources in 2015","text":"Europe's electricity generation by source in 2015.","size":"lg"}
```

### strip-plot

`<StripPlot>`, chart, category distribution. Shows every observation as a tick or dot along a value axis, one row per category.

Props:

- `value` (required): `string`. Numeric field positioning each mark.
- `group` (required): `string`. Category field: one row per distinct value.
- `label`: `string`. Field naming each observation, for the tooltip.
- `mark`: `"tick" | "dot"`, default `"tick"`. Thin vertical ticks (a barcode) or translucent dots.
- `median`: `boolean`, default `false`. Heavier tick at each row's median, with its value printed.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Order rows by median.
- `jitter`: `boolean`, default `false`. Deterministic vertical spread for dots, to relieve overplotting.

```json
{"type":"strip-plot","data":[{"day":"Mon","minutes":42},{"day":"Mon","minutes":44},{"day":"Mon","minutes":45},{"day":"Mon","minutes":47},{"day":"Mon","minutes":47},{"day":"Mon","minutes":48},{"day":"Mon","minutes":49},{"day":"Mon","minutes":51}],"value":"minutes","group":"day","median":true,"highlight":"Fri","format":"{value} min","title":"The median Friday commute took 40.5 minutes","subtitle":"Door-to-door commute time, 12 weeks of trips by weekday. The heavy tick is the median.","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### timeline-chart

`<TimelineChart>`, chart, category trend. Places events and spans on a time axis in labelled lanes, with each item named directly.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Label field: what the event or span is.
- `start` (required): `string`. Start field: ISO date, year or timestamp.
- `end`: `string`. End field. Rows without an end are point milestones.
- `lane`: `string`. Field that groups rows into labelled lanes.
- `precision`: `"year" | "month" | "day"`. Date precision in tooltips. Default: chosen from the span of the data.

```json
{"type":"timeline-chart","data":[{"mission":"Mercury","programme":"Crewed programmes","from":"1958-10","to":"1963-05"},{"mission":"Gemini","programme":"Crewed programmes","from":"1961-12","to":"1966-11"},{"mission":"Apollo","programme":"Crewed programmes","from":"1961-05","to":"1972-12"},{"mission":"Skylab","programme":"Crewed programmes","from":"1973-05","to":"1974-02"},{"mission":"Shuttle development","programme":"Crewed programmes","from":"1972-01","to":"1981-04"},{"mission":"Glenn orbits Earth","programme":"Milestones","from":"1962-02-20"},{"mission":"Apollo 1 fire","programme":"Milestones","from":"1967-01-27"},{"mission":"First Moon landing","programme":"Milestones","from":"1969-07-20"}],"name":"mission","start":"from","end":"to","lane":"programme","highlight":["Apollo","First Moon landing"],"title":"The Apollo programme ran from May 1961 to December 1972","subtitle":"NASA human spaceflight programmes and milestones, 1958 to 1981","source":"NASA History Office","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### treemap

`<Treemap>`, chart, category part-to-whole. Shows parts of a whole as nested rectangles sized by value, optionally grouped into categories.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Leaf name field: one tile per row.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: tile area. Non-positive values are dropped.
- `group`: `string`. Parent field. Rows sharing a group are drawn together and share a colour.
- `labels`: `boolean`, default `true`. Print the value under the name where the tile is big enough.
- `groupLabels`: `boolean`. Heading strip above each group. Default: on when `group` is set and not compact.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for group keys.

```json
{"type":"treemap","data":[{"sector":"Energy","source":"Electricity and heat","gt":15.8},{"sector":"Energy","source":"Transport","gt":8.4},{"sector":"Energy","source":"Manufacturing and construction","gt":6.3},{"sector":"Energy","source":"Buildings","gt":3},{"sector":"Energy","source":"Fugitive emissions","gt":3.3},{"sector":"Agriculture","source":"Livestock and manure","gt":3.5},{"sector":"Agriculture","source":"Soils and rice","gt":2.4},{"sector":"Industry","source":"Cement","gt":1.6}],"group":"sector","name":"source","value":"gt","format":"{value} Gt","title":"Energy produced 75% of global greenhouse gas emissions in 2021","subtitle":"Global emissions by sector and source, billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent, 2021","source":"Climate Watch, World Resources Institute","note":"Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### unit-blocks

`<UnitBlocks>`, chart, category poster. Shows the size of each group as a solid block of small icons, one icon per fixed number of units.

Props:

- `name` (required): `string`. Group field: one block of icons per row of data.
- `value` (required): `string`. Value field: the quantity each block counts out.
- `unit`: `number`. Units per icon. Default: a round number that gives about 2,000 icons in total.
- `unitLabel`: `string`. What one icon stands for, for the key line, e.g. "10 finishers".
- `icon`: `IconName | "path://..."`, default `"person"`. Built-in icon name or a custom single SVG path.
- `series`: `string`. Field that colours the blocks. Default: one colour per group, up to eight groups.
- `layout`: `"packed" | "columns"`, default `"packed"`. `packed`: equal block heights, widths follow the counts. `columns`: equal widths, blocks grow upwards from a baseline.
- `columns`: `number`. Blocks per line in the `columns` layout. Default: all, two on a phone.
- `iconSize`: `number`. Icon height in px. Default: the largest that fits, chosen per chart. To put two charts on one scale, give both the same `unit` and `iconSize`: the icon size, the gaps and the worth of an icon are then identical and the chart takes the height it needs.
- `sort`: `"none" | "asc" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Order of the blocks.

```json
{"type":"unit-blocks","data":[{"age":"Under 30","finishers":4180},{"age":"30 to 39","finishers":6920},{"age":"40 to 49","finishers":5340},{"age":"50 to 59","finishers":2760},{"age":"60 and over","finishers":1150}],"name":"age","value":"finishers","unit":10,"unitLabel":"10 finishers","format":"integer","title":"6,920 of the 20,350 finishers were aged 30 to 39","subtitle":"Finishers of the Lakeshore Marathon by age group, 2025","source":"Illustrative data","note":"Invented figures for a fictional race"}
```

### waffle-chart

`<WaffleChart>`, chart, category part-to-whole. Shows shares of a whole as counted cells in a grid, such as 37 in every 100.

Props:

- `value` (required): `string`. Value field. Each category's cells are its share of the whole.
- `name`: `string`. Category field. Omit for a single share.
- `total`: `number`. The whole. Default: the sum of the values. Set to 100 with one value to show a single share against an empty remainder.
- `rows`: `number`, default `10`. Grid rows.
- `columns`: `number`, default `10`. Grid columns.
- `shape`: `"square" | "circle"`, default `"square"`. Cell shape.
- `restLabel`: `string`. Label for the unfilled remainder when `total` exceeds the sum.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for category keys.

```json
{"type":"waffle-chart","data":[{"group":"Have never been online","share":33}],"name":"group","value":"share","total":100,"restLabel":"Use the internet","title":"33% of the world's population had never used the internet in 2023","subtitle":"Share of the global population, 2023. Each square is 1% of people","source":"ITU Facts and Figures 2023","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

## Molecules

### annotated-timeline

`<AnnotatedTimeline>`, HTML, category story. A vertical sequence of dated events along a rail, each with a short explanation and, optionally, a small chart or figure.

Composes: `step-marker`, `prose`, `sparkline`, `big-number`.

Props:

- `events` (required): `{ date, title, text?, figure?, emphasis? }[]`. The events in reading order. `date` is shown as written; `figure` is a chart spec or element; `emphasis` fills the marker to mark the most important events.
- `figurePosition`: `"below" | "side"`, default `"below"`. Where an event's figure sits; `side` falls back to `below` under 640px.
- `level`: `2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `3`. Heading level of the event titles.
- `title`: `string`. The main fact with its number, or a plain label.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Scope and period.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the timeline as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to every event.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"annotated-timeline","title":"The ECB raised its deposit rate from −0.5% to 4% between July 2022 and September 2023","subtitle":"Euro area deposit facility rate and annual inflation, 2021 to 2024","events":[{"date":"July 2021","title":"Inflation reaches 2.2%","text":"The ECB's target is 2%. The bank kept its deposit rate at −0.5%."},{"date":"July 2022","title":"The deposit rate rises from −0.5% to 0%","emphasis":true,"text":"This was the ECB's first rate rise in eleven years. Inflation was 8.9%.","figure":{"type":"big-number","value":"8.9%","label":"Annual inflation, July 2022","context":"The target is 2%"}},{"date":"October 2022","title":"Inflation reaches 10.6%","text":"This was the highest monthly figure of 2022. The ECB raised rates by 0.75 points at each of two consecutive meetings.","figure":{"type":"sparkline","data":[{"month":"2022-01","rate":5.1},{"month":"2022-02","rate":5.9},{"month":"2022-03","rate":7.4},{"month":"2022-04","rate":7.4},{"month":"2022-05","rate":8.1},{"month":"2022-06","rate":8.6},{"month":"2022-07","rate":8.9},{"month":"2022-08","rate":9.1},{"month":"2022-09","rate":9.9},{"month":"2022-10","rate":10.6},{"month":"2022-11","rate":10.1},{"month":"2022-12","rate":9.2}],"x":"month","y":"rate","format":"{value}%","extremes":true,"showValue":true,"style":{"maxWidth":260}}},{"date":"September 2023","title":"The deposit rate reaches 4%","text":"This was the tenth rise in a row. Inflation was 4.3%."},{"date":"June 2024","title":"The deposit rate is cut to 3.75%","emphasis":true,"text":"The cut was 0.25 points. Inflation was 2.5%."}],"source":"European Central Bank; Eurostat","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### before-after

`<BeforeAfter>`, HTML, category layout. Two states of one measure side by side, as figures or small charts, with the change between them stated in the middle.

Composes: `big-number`, `delta`, `bar-chart`, `sparkline`.

Props:

- `before` (required): `{ heading?, value?, label?, context?, format?, chart? }`. The first state: a figure, a chart slot, or both.
- `after` (required): `{ heading?, value?, label?, context?, format?, chart? }`. The second state.
- `delta`: `number | string`. The change stated between the two. Default: the relative change when both values are numbers.
- `deltaLabel`: `string`. Words under the change, e.g. "in five years".
- `deltaFormat`: `FormatSpec`, default `signed percent`. Number format for a numeric `delta`.
- `upIsGood`: `boolean`, default `true`. Whether an increase is good news; decides the colour of the change.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"auto"`. Number format shared by both values.
- `title`: `string`. The change stated plainly, with both values and the period.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Measure and population.
- `source`: `string`. Shown underneath as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to both states.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"before-after","title":"Solar module prices fell from $0.74 to $0.15 per watt between 2013 and 2023","subtitle":"Average price of crystalline silicon modules, US dollars per watt","format":{"style":"currency","currency":"USD"},"before":{"heading":"2013","value":0.74,"label":"Per watt","context":"2013 average"},"after":{"heading":"2023","value":0.15,"label":"Per watt","context":"2023 average"},"deltaLabel":"in ten years","upIsGood":false,"source":"IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2023","note":"Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"}
```

### chart-callout

`<ChartCallout>`, HTML, category layout. A chart with a callout beside it that states the main fact. In narrow containers the callout goes underneath.

Composes: `callout`, `line-chart`, `bar-chart`.

Props:

- `chart` (required): `Slot`. The chart: a spec or a React element.
- `lead`: `string`. The main fact in a few words, with its number. Shown in bold.
- `body`: `string`. One or two plain sentences that say what the fact means.
- `tone`: `"neutral" | "positive" | "negative" | "accent"`, default `"accent"`. Sets the callout's icon and tint together.
- `label`: `string`. Small label above the lead, e.g. "Takeaway" or "Caveat".
- `side`: `"left" | "right"`, default `"right"`. Side of the chart the callout sits on. Under 640px it always goes underneath.
- `variant`: `"plain" | "soft" | "outline"`, default `"plain"`. `plain` separates the callout with a hairline; the others box it.
- `align`: `"start" | "center" | "end"`, default `"center"`. Vertical position of the callout beside the chart.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `chart`.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the chart and callout.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"chart-callout","chart":{"type":"line-chart","data":[{"month":"2024-01-01","rate":4.2},{"month":"2024-02-01","rate":4.3},{"month":"2024-03-01","rate":4.1},{"month":"2024-04-01","rate":3.6},{"month":"2024-05-01","rate":3.1},{"month":"2024-06-01","rate":2.9},{"month":"2024-07-01","rate":2.6},{"month":"2024-08-01","rate":2.4},{"month":"2024-09-01","rate":2.3},{"month":"2024-10-01","rate":2.2},{"month":"2024-11-01","rate":2.1},{"month":"2024-12-01","rate":2.1}],"x":"month","y":"rate","format":"{value}%","zero":true,"height":280,"title":"Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024","subtitle":"Monthly customer churn, 2024","source":"Internal analytics","note":"Illustrative data","annotations":[{"type":"line","axis":"x","value":"2024-03-01","label":"New onboarding"}]},"label":"Takeaway","lead":"Churn fell 2 points after March","body":"Churn was 4.1% in March, when the new onboarding launched. It fell every month from April to November. It was 2.1% in December."}
```

### chart-tabs

`<ChartTabs>`, HTML, category layout. One chart frame with a segmented control that switches between several views of the same data, morphing between views that share a chart type.

Composes: `bar-chart`, `line-chart`.

Props:

- `chart`: `InsightSpec`. The base chart spec every view starts from: `{ type, data, ... }`.
- `views` (required): `{ label, id?, props?, chart? }[]`. Two to five views. `props` are merged over `chart`; or give a view its own complete `chart` slot.
- `defaultView`: `string | number`. The view shown first: an id, a label or an index.
- `view`: `string | number`. Controlled active view.
- `onViewChange`: `(id, index) => void`. Called when the reader switches view.
- `tabsLabel`: `string`, default `"Chart view"`. Accessible name of the tab list.
- `tabsPosition`: `"right" | "below"`, default `"right"`. Tabs beside the title or under it. Under 560px they always go underneath.
- `title`: `string`. A plain label or fact that is true of every view.
- `subtitle`: `string`. What the views share; each view's own `subtitle` names its measure.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the chart as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Extra content under the chart.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the chart.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"chart-tabs","title":"CO2 emissions of six large emitters, 2023","tabsPosition":"below","chart":{"type":"bar-chart","data":[{"country":"China","total":11.9,"perCapita":8.4,"change":0.38},{"country":"United States","total":4.9,"perCapita":14.3,"change":-0.13},{"country":"India","total":3.1,"perCapita":2.1,"change":0.74},{"country":"Russia","total":1.8,"perCapita":12.5,"change":0.1},{"country":"Japan","total":1,"perCapita":8,"change":-0.19},{"country":"Germany","total":0.6,"perCapita":7.1,"change":-0.28}],"x":"country","y":"total","sort":"desc","orientation":"horizontal","height":280,"highlight":"China","format":"{value} Gt","subtitle":"CO2 emissions from fossil fuels, billion tonnes, 2023"},"views":[{"label":"Total","id":"total"},{"label":"Per capita","id":"per-capita","props":{"y":"perCapita","highlight":"United States","format":"{value} t","subtitle":"CO2 emissions per person, tonnes, 2023"}},{"label":"Change since 2010","id":"change","props":{"y":"change","highlight":"India","format":"percent","subtitle":"Change in CO2 emissions, 2010 to 2023"}}],"source":"Global Carbon Budget 2024","note":"Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"}
```

### comparison-table

`<ComparisonTable>`, HTML, category layout. A table whose rows carry inline sparklines, deltas and in-cell bars beside their exact values, from rows and a column config.

Composes: `sparkline`, `delta`.

Props:

- `data`: `DataInput`. Wide data: one row per entity. Long data: one row per entity and period, with `groupBy`. Omit inside `<InsightData>`.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied before rows are grouped.
- `columns` (required): `(string | { key, label?, kind?, fields?, agg?, change?, format?, upIsGood?, mark?, align?, width?, hideBelow?, sortable? })[]`. Columns in order; the first is the row header. `kind` is `text`, `number`, `sparkline`, `delta` or `bar`. For wide data give a sparkline or computed delta its series with `fields`; for long data they use the group's rows.
- `groupBy`: `string`. Long data: the entity field. Rows sharing a value become one table row, in data order.
- `highlight`: `string | string[]`. Entities to emphasise, matched on the first column.
- `sort`: `{ key, direction?: "asc" | "desc" }`. Order rows by a column's value. Default direction: descending. With `sortable` this is the opening order.
- `sortable`: `boolean`, default `true`. Click or press Enter on a column header to sort by it (numbers largest first, text A to Z); a second press reverses and a third restores the original order. Sparkline columns do not sort; set `sortable: false` on a column to exclude it.
- `limit`: `number`. Show only the first N rows.
- `density`: `"comfortable" | "compact"`, default `"comfortable"`. Row padding.
- `title`: `string`. The main fact with its number, or a plain label. Set as the table's `<caption>`.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Units and period.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the table as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the sparklines and deltas.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"comparison-table","title":"The Netherlands' renewable share of electricity rose from 18.2% to 52.4% between 2019 and 2024","subtitle":"Renewable share of electricity generation, selected EU countries, 2019 to 2024","data":[{"2019":40.1,"2020":44.2,"2021":40.9,"2022":44.5,"2023":52.6,"2024":58.9,"country":"Germany","share":58.9,"twh":498},{"2019":37.5,"2020":44.1,"2021":46.7,"2022":42.2,"2023":50.3,"2024":56.8,"country":"Spain","share":56.8,"twh":264},{"2019":18.2,"2020":26.1,"2021":33,"2022":40.1,"2023":47.7,"2024":52.4,"country":"Netherlands","share":52.4,"twh":121},{"2019":39.9,"2020":41.7,"2021":40.3,"2022":35.6,"2023":43.8,"2024":49,"country":"Italy","share":49,"twh":264},{"2019":20.9,"2020":24.2,"2021":22.5,"2022":24.4,"2023":27,"2024":28.3,"country":"France","share":28.3,"twh":536},{"2019":14.1,"2020":17.2,"2021":16.9,"2022":20.6,"2023":26.4,"2024":29.5,"country":"Poland","share":29.5,"twh":167}],"columns":[{"key":"country","label":"Country"},{"key":"twh","label":"Generation, TWh","kind":"bar","format":"integer","hideBelow":560},{"key":"share","label":"Share, 2024","format":"{value}%"},{"key":"trend","label":"2019 to 2024","kind":"sparkline","fields":["2019","2020","2021","2022","2023","2024"],"format":"{value}%"},{"key":"change","label":"Change","kind":"delta","fields":["2019","2020","2021","2022","2023","2024"],"change":"absolute","format":"{value} pts"}],"sort":{"key":"share"},"highlight":"Netherlands","source":"Ember, European Electricity Review 2025","note":"Rounded, illustrative"}
```

### filter-chips

`<FilterChips>`, HTML, category layout. The active crossfilter selections of the surrounding `InsightData`, shown as removable chips with a reset control.

Props:

- `selections`: `Record<string, { field, values?, range? }>`. Selections to show when there is no surrounding `<InsightData>` (or to override it), keyed by owner. Uncontrolled unless `onSelectionsChange` is given.
- `onSelectionsChange`: `(selections) => void`. Called when a chip is removed or the reset is pressed; makes `selections` controlled.
- `labels`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for field names, e.g. `{ region: "Region" }`.
- `hint`: `string`. Shown while nothing is selected, e.g. "Click a bar to filter".
- `resetLabel`: `string`, default `"Reset"`. Text of the clear-all control.
- `count`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show "1,204 of 5,000 rows" at the end of the line.
- `unit`: `string`, default `"rows"`. Noun for the count, e.g. "orders".
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"filter-chips","labels":{"region":"Region","source":"Source","year":"Year"},"selections":{"by-region":{"field":"region","values":["Asia","Europe"]},"by-source":{"field":"source","values":["Solar"]},"by-year":{"field":"year","range":[2020,2024]}}}
```

### hero-figure
