`<HeroFigure>`, HTML, category story. The opening exhibit of a piece: kicker, headline and deck above one large chart, with a source line underneath.

Composes: `headline`, `source-note`, `line-chart`, `big-number`.

Props:

- `title` (required): `string`. The main fact, as one plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the series or topic.
- `deck`: `string`. One plain sentence under the title that adds a second fact.
- `byline`: `string`. Author line, e.g. "By Ana Ruiz".
- `date`: `string`. Publication date. ISO dates are formatted for the locale.
- `chart` (required): `Slot`. The hero chart: a spec or a React element, without its own title.
- `source`: `string | { name, url? } | (string | { name, url? })[]`. Where the data comes from. Entries with a `url` are linked.
- `period`: `string`. The period the data covers.
- `note`: `string`. Caveats the reader should know.
- `align`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Headline alignment.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `1`. Heading level of the title.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `chart`.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the headline, chart and source note.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"hero-figure","kicker":"Energy transition","title":"Solar supplied 11.1% of EU electricity in 2024","deck":"Coal's share fell from 24.6% in 2015 to 9.8% in 2024.","byline":"By Ana Ruiz","date":"2025-01-23","chart":{"type":"line-chart","data":[{"year":"2015","Solar":2.9,"Coal":24.6},{"year":"2016","Solar":3,"Coal":22},{"year":"2017","Solar":3.4,"Coal":20.6},{"year":"2018","Solar":3.7,"Coal":19.2},{"year":"2019","Solar":4.2,"Coal":15},{"year":"2020","Solar":5,"Coal":13},{"year":"2021","Solar":5.4,"Coal":14.7},{"year":"2022","Solar":7,"Coal":15.8},{"year":"2023","Solar":9.1,"Coal":12.3},{"year":"2024","Solar":11.1,"Coal":9.8}],"x":"year","y":["Solar","Coal"],"format":"{value}%","zero":true,"height":380,"subtitle":"Solar and coal share of EU electricity generation, 2015 to 2024","annotations":[{"type":"point","x":"2024","y":11.1,"label":"Solar 11.1%","position":"left"}]},"source":{"name":"Ember, European Electricity Review 2025","url":"https://ember-energy.org"},"note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration","period":"2015 to 2024"}
```

### kpi-grid

`<KpiGrid>`, HTML, category layout. A responsive grid of trend cards drawn from one dataset: each metric shows its latest value, its change and a sparkline.

Composes: `trend-card`.

Props:

- `data`: `DataInput`. One dataset in time order: a row per period, a column per metric. Omit inside `<InsightData>`.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied once, before the cards read the rows.
- `x`: `string`. Period field shared by every metric.
- `metrics` (required): `{ y, label, format?, upIsGood?, compare?, change?, deltaFormat?, deltaLabel?, context?, value?, delta?, kind? }[]`. One card per metric; each takes the props of `trend-card`.
- `compare`: `"first" | "previous" | number`, default `"first"`. Baseline for every card's change; a metric can override it.
- `change`: `"percent" | "absolute"`, default `"percent"`. Relative change, or the difference between the two values; a metric can override it. An absolute change of a percentage metric is shown in percentage points ("−2.1 pts").
- `deltaFormat`: `FormatSpec`. Format for absolute changes, e.g. `"{value} pp"` or `"signed"`; a metric can override it. Default: points for percentage formats, otherwise the metric's own `format`.
- `columns`: `number`. Preferred columns. Default: up to four, reduced to fit cards of at least 200px.
- `title`: `string`. The main fact with its number, or a plain label.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Population and period.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the grid as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to every card.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"kpi-grid","title":"Monthly active users rose from 38,100 to 48,200 in 2024","subtitle":"Four product metrics by month, 2024. Change is measured against January.","data":[{"month":"2024-01-01","users":38100,"mrr":412000,"churn":4.2,"response":4.1},{"month":"2024-02-01","users":39400,"mrr":428000,"churn":4,"response":3.9},{"month":"2024-03-01","users":39000,"mrr":431000,"churn":3.9,"response":3.8},{"month":"2024-04-01","users":40800,"mrr":455000,"churn":3.6,"response":3.2},{"month":"2024-05-01","users":42200,"mrr":470000,"churn":3.1,"response":3.4},{"month":"2024-06-01","users":41900,"mrr":476000,"churn":2.9,"response":2.9},{"month":"2024-07-01","users":43500,"mrr":498000,"churn":2.6,"response":2.7},{"month":"2024-08-01","users":44100,"mrr":511000,"churn":2.4,"response":2.6}],"x":"month","metrics":[{"y":"users","label":"Monthly active users","format":"compact"},{"y":"mrr","label":"Recurring revenue","format":"currency:USD"},{"y":"churn","label":"Monthly churn","format":"{value}%","change":"absolute","upIsGood":false},{"y":"response","label":"Median first response","format":"{value} h","upIsGood":false}],"source":"Internal analytics","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### linked-charts

`<LinkedCharts>`, HTML, category layout. Two to four charts over one shared dataset in a responsive grid: clicking a mark in one filters the others, with the active filters shown as removable chips.

Composes: `filter-chips`, `bar-chart`, `line-chart`.

Props:

- `data` (required): `DataInput`. The shared, row-level dataset.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied once to the shared data.
- `charts`: `Slot[]`. Two to four chart specs or elements. Give each `select: true` (or a field name) and a stable `id`, and leave out `data`.
- `columns`: `number`. Preferred columns. Default two; fewer when charts would be narrower than `minChartWidth`.
- `minChartWidth`: `number`, default `260`. Narrowest a chart may get before the grid drops a column.
- `filters`: `boolean`, default `true`. Show the filter line (`filter-chips`).
- `hint`: `string`, default `"Click a mark to filter the other charts"`. Shown in the filter line while nothing is selected.
- `labels`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for the fields in the chips.
- `count`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show the filtered row count at the end of the filter line.
- `unit`: `string`, default `"rows"`. Noun for the count.
- `selections`: `Record<string, Selection>`. Controlled selections, keyed by chart id.
- `onSelectionsChange`: `(selections) => void`. Called when the selections change.
- `title`: `string`. Heading for the group.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Measure, population and period shared by the charts.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the grid as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `charts`.
- `before`: `Slot | Slot[]`. Content rendered inside the shared store above the grid: figures, text, a custom component that calls `useInsightData()`, or a spec that omits `data` (e.g. `stat-row`, `data-table`). It sees the same filtered rows as the charts.
- `after`: `Slot | Slot[]`. Content rendered inside the shared store below the grid, e.g. a detail table of the filtered rows.
- `gap`: `number`, default `24`. Space in px between the `before` slot, the grid and the `after` slot.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to every chart.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"linked-charts","title":"Asia generated 46% of the renewable electricity in these four regions from 2020 to 2024","subtitle":"Electricity generation from hydro, wind and solar, TWh, four regions, 2020 to 2024","data":[{"region":"Asia","year":"2020","source":"Hydro","twh":1810},{"region":"Asia","year":"2020","source":"Wind","twh":480},{"region":"Asia","year":"2020","source":"Solar","twh":420},{"region":"Asia","year":"2021","source":"Hydro","twh":1790},{"region":"Asia","year":"2021","source":"Wind","twh":590},{"region":"Asia","year":"2021","source":"Solar","twh":560},{"region":"Asia","year":"2022","source":"Hydro","twh":1830},{"region":"Asia","year":"2022","source":"Wind","twh":700}],"labels":{"region":"Region","source":"Source","year":"Year"},"hint":"Click a bar to filter the other charts","count":true,"charts":[{"type":"bar-chart","id":"by-region","x":"region","y":"twh","select":true,"format":"compact","height":200,"title":"By region","transform":{"type":"aggregate","groupBy":"region","measures":{"twh":{"op":"sum","field":"twh"}}}},{"type":"bar-chart","id":"by-source","x":"source","y":"twh","select":true,"format":"compact","height":200,"title":"By source","transform":{"type":"aggregate","groupBy":"source","measures":{"twh":{"op":"sum","field":"twh"}}}},{"type":"bar-chart","id":"by-year","x":"year","y":"twh","series":"source","stack":true,"orientation":"vertical","sort":"none","select":"year","format":"compact","height":240,"title":"By year","transform":{"type":"aggregate","groupBy":["year","source"],"measures":{"twh":{"op":"sum","field":"twh"}}}}],"source":"Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025","note":"Regional figures rounded, illustrative"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### metric-breakdown

`<MetricBreakdown>`, HTML, category layout. A headline number with its composition underneath: one segmented bar and a key giving each part's value and share.

Composes: `big-number`, `segmented-bar`.

Props:

- `label` (required): `string`. What the headline number measures.
- `data`: `DataInput`. One row per part. Omit inside `<InsightData>`.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied before the parts are summed.
- `name` (required): `string`. Field naming each part.
- `value` (required): `string`. Field with each part's value.
- `total`: `number | string`. The headline number. Default: the sum of the parts.
- `context`: `string`. The line under the headline number.
- `delta`: `number | string`. Change in the headline number. Numbers render as signed percentages.
- `deltaLabel`: `string`. What the delta is against.
- `upIsGood`: `boolean`, default `true`. Whether an increase is good news.
- `size`: `"hero" | "stat"`, default `"stat"`. `hero` when this opens a piece.
- `show`: `"both" | "value" | "share"`, default `"both"`. What the key prints beside each part.
- `sort`: `"none" | "desc"`, default `"none"`. Order parts by size; the bar and the key follow.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for part keys.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"auto"`. Number format for the headline and the parts.
- `source`: `string`. Shown underneath as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the number and the bar.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"metric-breakdown","label":"Greenhouse gas emissions, EU-27, 2022","context":"Million tonnes of CO2 equivalent. 31% below the 1990 level.","data":[{"sector":"Energy supply","mt":862},{"sector":"Transport","mt":804},{"sector":"Industry","mt":701},{"sector":"Buildings","mt":437},{"sector":"Agriculture","mt":378},{"sector":"Waste","mt":109}],"name":"sector","value":"mt","format":"integer","source":"European Environment Agency","note":"Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"}
```

### poster

`<Poster>`, HTML, category poster. The sheet an infographic is composed on. It paints a full-bleed ground from a poster theme, forces one theme and colour mode on everything inside, and lays out a masthead, a grid of panels and a footer. It can save the whole sheet as one PNG.

Composes: `big-number`, `pictogram-chart`, `bar-chart`, `donut-chart`, `treemap`, `waffle-chart`, `segmented-bar`, `icon-stat`.

Props:

- `title`: `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. Set large and light in the theme's display face.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic or series.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One or two lines under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `panels` (required): `PosterPanel[]`. The blocks, in reading order. Each is `{ content, title?, subtitle?, span?, rowSpan?, source?, note?, align?, valign?, bleed?, id? }`. `content` is a component spec or rendered content. `span` is in units of `columns` (default: full width). `bleed` runs the content to the poster's left and right edges.
- `columns`: `number`, default `12`. Columns of the layout grid: a 12-unit grid, or a simple count such as 2 or 3. Under 600px every panel is full width; from 600 to 760px the grid has two columns.
- `gap`: `number`. Space between panels in px. Default 40 (28 under 600px).
- `padding`: `number`. Space between the poster's edge and its content in px. Default 56 (36 under 900px, 20 under 600px).
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1200`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `aspect`: `number | string`. Fixed shape as width / height: `0.75`, `"3:4"`, `"16:9"`. The poster still grows when its content needs more height, and the ratio is dropped under 600px.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"noir"`. A poster theme name, any other theme name, or a theme object. It is passed on to everything inside.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `background`: `string`. CSS background of the sheet, a colour or a gradient. Default: the poster theme's ground. Keep it close to the theme's `surface`, which charts use for the gaps between marks.
- `rules`: `"none" | "solid" | "dotted"`, default `"dotted"`. Lines under the masthead, between rows of panels and above the footer.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `titleAlign`: `"left" | "center"`, default `"left"`. Alignment of the masthead.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster. The image is the whole sheet, drawn from the DOM onto a canvas, without the control.
- `exportWidth`: `number`, default `2400`. Width of the downloaded PNG in pixels.
- `filename`: `string`. File name without extension. Defaults to a slug of the title.
- `downloadLabel`: `string`, default `"Download PNG"`. Label of the download control.
- `onExport`: `(blob: Blob) => void`. Called with the PNG after a download.

```json
{"type":"poster","theme":"noir","kicker":"Transport","title":"Riverton's bike-share scheme carried 4.2 million trips in 2025","subtitle":"Trips, bikes and reasons for riding in the city's public bike-share scheme, January to December 2025.","panels":[{"span":4,"valign":"center","content":{"type":"big-number","size":"hero","value":"4.2 million","label":"Trips in 2025","context":"3.4 million in 2024"}},{"span":8,"title":"Old Town had 1,150 of the scheme's 3,000 bikes","content":{"type":"pictogram-chart","data":[{"district":"Old Town","bikes":1150},{"district":"Harbour","bikes":820},{"district":"University","bikes":640},{"district":"Northside","bikes":390}],"name":"district","value":"bikes","unit":50,"unitLabel":"50 bikes","icon":"bike","highlight":"Old Town"},"source":"Riverton Transport Office"},{"span":7,"title":"670,000 trips were made on Wednesdays in 2025","subtitle":"Trips by day of the week, thousands, 2025","content":{"type":"bar-chart","data":[{"day":"Mon","trips":610},{"day":"Tue","trips":655},{"day":"Wed","trips":670},{"day":"Thu","trips":662},{"day":"Fri","trips":640},{"day":"Sat","trips":520},{"day":"Sun","trips":443}],"x":"day","y":"trips","orientation":"vertical","sort":"none","highlight":"Wed","format":"{value}k","height":260}},{"span":5,"title":"46% of trips were commutes","subtitle":"Share of trips by stated purpose, rider survey, 2025","content":{"type":"donut-chart","data":[{"purpose":"Commuting","share":46},{"purpose":"Leisure","share":27},{"purpose":"Errands","share":18},{"purpose":"Other","share":9}],"name":"purpose","value":"share","format":"{value}%","centerValue":"46%","centerLabel":"Commuting","height":260}}],"sources":["Riverton Transport Office","Riverton rider survey 2025"],"note":"Riverton is an invented city. All figures are illustrative.","credit":"InsightCharts"}
```

### proportion-statement

`<ProportionStatement>`, HTML, category story. A share stated as a countable sentence ("37 in every 100…"): a waffle grid or a row of icons beside the statement in large type, with the number emphasised.

Composes: `waffle-chart`, `icon-stat`.

Props:

- `value` (required): `number`. How many of the whole are counted.
- `total`: `number`, default `100`. The whole.
- `figure`: `string`. The emphasised words. Default: "{value} in every {total}", or "{value} in {total}" up to 20.
- `text` (required): `string`. The rest of the sentence, read straight after the figure.
- `visual`: `"waffle" | "icons"`. Grid of cells or row of glyphs. Default: icons up to a total of 20, waffle above.
- `icon`: `"circle" | "person" | "square"`, default `"person"`. Glyph for the `icons` visual.
- `shape`: `"square" | "circle"`, default `"square"`. Cell shape for the `waffle` visual.
- `side`: `"left" | "right"`, default `"left"`. Side the visual sits on; under 520px it goes on top.
- `detail`: `string`. A second, quieter sentence under the statement.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the statement as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the visual.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"proportion-statement","value":33,"total":100,"text":"people in the world have never used the internet.","detail":"That was about 2.6 billion people in 2023.","source":"ITU Facts and Figures 2023","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### quote-figure

`<QuoteFigure>`, HTML, category story. A pull-quote paired with the statistic or small chart that backs it up, side by side and stacking in narrow containers.

Composes: `pull-quote`, `big-number`, `sparkline`.

Props:

- `quote` (required): `string`. The words quoted, without quotation marks.
- `attribution`: `string`. Who said it.
- `role`: `string`. Their role, or where it was said.
- `cite`: `string`. Source URL, linked from the attribution.
- `stat`: `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format? }`. The statistic that backs the quote up; takes the props of `big-number`.
- `figure`: `Slot`. A small chart or figure instead of, or under, the statistic: a spec or a React element.
- `side`: `"left" | "right"`, default `"right"`. Side the evidence sits on; under 640px it goes underneath.
- `source`: `string`. Shown underneath as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the quote and the figure.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"quote-figure","quote":"Solar met more than half of demand on 41% of summer afternoons in 2024. We do not have enough storage for the midday surplus yet.","attribution":"Marta Keller","role":"Grid planner, quoted in the 2024 system adequacy review","stat":{"value":0.41,"format":"percent","label":"Summer afternoons when solar met over half of demand","context":"It was 6% of afternoons in 2019"},"figure":{"type":"sparkline","data":[{"year":"2019","share":6},{"year":"2020","share":9},{"year":"2021","share":14},{"year":"2022","share":22},{"year":"2023","share":31},{"year":"2024","share":41}],"x":"year","y":"share","format":"{value}%","area":true},"source":"National grid operator, hourly generation data","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

### ranked-list

`<RankedList>`, HTML, category layout. A ranking as a list: position, name, value and a thin in-row bar, with an optional change indicator and highlighted rows.

Composes: `delta`.

Props:

- `data`: `DataInput`. One row per entity. Omit inside `<InsightData>`.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied before ranking.
- `name` (required): `string`. Field naming each entity.
- `value` (required): `string`. Field with the value that ranks them. Bars start at zero.
- `change`: `string`. Field with a change shown at the end of each row: a number (0.12 is +12%) or a string.
- `changeFormat`: `FormatSpec`, default `signed percent`. Format for numeric changes, e.g. `"signed"` for places moved.
- `upIsGood`: `boolean`, default `true`. Whether a positive change is good news.
- `detail`: `string`. Field with a short secondary line under each name.
- `sort`: `"desc" | "asc" | "none"`, default `"desc"`. Order by value; `none` keeps the data order.
- `limit`: `number`. Show only the first N rows after sorting.
- `highlight`: `string | string[]`. Entity names to emphasise. The other bars are drawn in grey.
- `bar`: `boolean`, default `true`. Draw the in-row bar.
- `max`: `number`. Value at which a bar is full. Default: the largest value shown.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"auto"`. Number format for the values.
- `title`: `string`. The main fact with its number, or a plain label.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Measure, population and period.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the list as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"ranked-list","title":"11% of commuting trips in Paris are made by bicycle","subtitle":"Share of commuting trips made by bicycle, selected European cities, with change since 2019","data":[{"city":"Copenhagen","country":"Denmark","share":49,"change":0.04},{"city":"Amsterdam","country":"Netherlands","share":35,"change":0.01},{"city":"Utrecht","country":"Netherlands","share":34,"change":0.02},{"city":"Münster","country":"Germany","share":31,"change":0},{"city":"Antwerp","country":"Belgium","share":26,"change":0.05},{"city":"Malmö","country":"Sweden","share":25,"change":-0.01},{"city":"Bordeaux","country":"France","share":13,"change":0.06},{"city":"Paris","country":"France","share":11,"change":0.07}],"name":"city","detail":"country","value":"share","format":"{value}%","change":"change","highlight":"Paris","source":"City mobility surveys","note":"Illustrative data"}
```

### scrolly-chart

`<ScrollyChart>`, HTML, category story. A scroll-driven story from JSON: one base chart spec and a list of steps, each with narration and a patch of chart props applied while that step is active.

Composes: `prose`, `bar-chart`.

Props:

- `chart` (required): `InsightSpec`. The base chart spec: `{ type, data, x, y, ... }`. Give it a `title`; steps may replace it.
- `steps` (required): `{ content, id?, label?, ...chart props }[]`. The steps in order. `content` is a short paragraph that says plainly what the chart now shows (`**bold**` works). Every other key is a chart prop merged over `chart` for that step: `highlight`, `transform`, `annotations`, `x`, `y`, `title`… Use `null` to remove a base prop. Change one thing per step.
- `cumulative`: `boolean`, default `false`. Each step's patch builds on the previous steps instead of on the base spec alone.
- `scrollMode`: `"auto" | "scroll" | "swipe" | "steps"`, default `"auto"`. `scroll` pins the chart while steps scroll past; `swipe` makes steps swipeable cards; `steps` shows previous/next buttons; `auto` uses scroll, or swipe on narrow touch screens. (Named `scrollMode` because `mode` is the colour mode.)
- `side`: `"left" | "right"`, default `"left"`. Side of the text column in scroll mode. Narrow containers overlay the text on the chart.
- `stickyTop`: `number | string`, default `0`. Offset from the top of the viewport at which the chart pins; set it to the height of a fixed header.
- `stepHeight`: `string`, default `"80vh"`. Scroll distance per step, as a CSS length.
- `onStepChange`: `(index) => void`. Called when the active step changes.
- `title`: `string`. Heading above the whole story.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Line under the heading.
- `source`: `string`. Shown after the last step as "Source: ...". Prefer the chart's own `source`, which stays visible.
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the chart and the step cards.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"scrolly-chart","chart":{"type":"bar-chart","data":[{"source":"Coal","y2015":24.6,"y2024":9.8},{"source":"Gas","y2015":15.8,"y2024":15.7},{"source":"Nuclear","y2015":27.1,"y2024":23.7},{"source":"Wind","y2015":9.2,"y2024":17.4},{"source":"Hydro","y2015":12,"y2024":13.2},{"source":"Solar","y2015":2.9,"y2024":11.1}],"x":"source","y":"y2015","sort":"none","orientation":"horizontal","format":"{value}%","height":300,"title":"EU electricity generation by source, 2015","subtitle":"Share of EU electricity generation, %","source":"Ember, European Electricity Review 2025","note":"Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"},"steps":[{"id":"baseline","label":"2015","content":"In 2015 **nuclear and coal** together supplied 51.7% of the EU's electricity."},{"id":"coal","content":"Coal supplied 24.6% in 2015. Only nuclear supplied more.","highlight":"Coal"},{"id":"today","label":"2024","content":"In 2024 coal supplied 9.8%.","highlight":"Coal","y":"y2024","title":"EU electricity generation by source, 2024"},{"id":"solar","content":"**Solar** supplied 11.1% in 2024. It supplied 2.9% in 2015.","highlight":"Solar","y":"y2024","title":"Solar supplied 11.1% of EU electricity in 2024"}],"stepHeight":"70vh","stickyTop":16}
```

### section

`<Section>`, HTML, category story. A story section: a numbered step marker or a headline, introductory prose, then one or more exhibits in a responsive one- to three-column grid.

Composes: `step-marker`, `headline`, `prose`, `line-chart`, `bar-chart`, `stat-tile`.

Props:

- `title`: `string`. The section's main fact, as one plain sentence with its number.
- `step`: `number | string`. Step number: turns the heading into a numbered chapter marker ("02 — ...").
- `total`: `number`. Total steps, shown as "02 / 05".
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above an unnumbered heading.
- `deck`: `string`. One plain sentence under the heading that adds a second fact.
- `intro`: `string | string[]`. Introductory narration. Supports `**bold**`, `*italic*` and links.
- `body`: `Slot | Slot[]`. The exhibits: one slot or several, each a spec or a React element.
- `columns`: `1 | 2 | 3`, default `1`. Columns for the body at full width; reduced under 720px and 520px.
- `outro`: `string | string[]`. Closing narration under the body.
- `rule`: `boolean`, default `false`. Hairline above the section.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `2`. Heading level.
- `id`: `string`. Anchor id for deep links.
- `spacing`: `"compact" | "comfortable"`, default `"comfortable"`. Vertical rhythm between heading, intro and body.
- `children`: `ReactNode`. JSX alternative to `body`; each child becomes a grid item.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to everything inside.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"section","step":2,"total":4,"title":"First-quarter churn was 2.0% for customers who joined after March","intro":"Monthly churn fell from 4.2% in January to 2.1% in December 2024. The new onboarding launched in March. Customers who joined after March had first-quarter churn of **2.0%**. Customers who joined before March had 4.1%.","columns":2,"body":[{"type":"line-chart","data":[{"month":"2024-01-01","rate":4.2},{"month":"2024-02-01","rate":4.3},{"month":"2024-03-01","rate":4.1},{"month":"2024-04-01","rate":3.6},{"month":"2024-05-01","rate":3.1},{"month":"2024-06-01","rate":2.9},{"month":"2024-07-01","rate":2.6},{"month":"2024-08-01","rate":2.4},{"month":"2024-09-01","rate":2.3},{"month":"2024-10-01","rate":2.2},{"month":"2024-11-01","rate":2.1},{"month":"2024-12-01","rate":2.1}],"x":"month","y":"rate","format":"{value}%","zero":true,"height":240,"title":"Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024","subtitle":"Monthly customer churn, 2024","annotations":[{"type":"line","axis":"x","value":"2024-03-01","label":"New onboarding"}]},{"type":"bar-chart","data":[{"cohort":"Before March","churn":4.1},{"cohort":"After March","churn":2}],"x":"cohort","y":"churn","format":"{value}%","height":240,"highlight":"After March","title":"First-quarter churn was 4.1% for customers who joined before March","subtitle":"First-quarter churn by sign-up cohort, 2024"}],"outro":"The next section covers the first 90 days after sign-up."}
```

### small-multiple-grid

`<SmallMultipleGrid>`, HTML, category layout. Repeats any chart spec once per value of a facet field, each panel with its own filtered rows and a title, in a grid that follows the container width.

Composes: `legend-key`, `bar-chart`, `waffle-chart`.

Props:

- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows for every panel together. Omit inside `<InsightData>`.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied before the rows are split by `facet`.
- `facet` (required): `string`. Field whose values each get a panel.
- `chart` (required): `InsightSpec | (facet, rows) => ReactNode`. The chart repeated in every panel: a spec without `data` and without a `title`, or a render function from JSX.
- `columns`: `number`. Preferred columns. Default: up to four, reduced to fit `minPanelWidth`.
- `minPanelWidth`: `number`, default `200`. Narrowest a panel may get before the grid drops a column.
- `order`: `"data" | "asc" | "desc" | string[]`, default `"data"`. Panel order: data order, alphabetical, or an explicit list of facet values.
- `panelHeight`: `number`, default `160`. Plot height of each panel when the spec sets none.
- `highlight`: `string | string[]`. Passed to every panel as its `highlight`, so the same entity is emphasised everywhere.
- `emphasis`: `string | string[]`. Facet values whose panel titles are emphasised.
- `legend`: `(string | { label, color?, index?, shape?, muted? })[]`. One shared colour key above the panels (`legend-key` items, in series order). Set `legend: false` in the chart spec so panels do not repeat it.
- `names`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for facet values.
- `level`: `2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `4`. Heading level of the panel titles.
- `title`: `string`. The main fact with its number, or a plain label.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Measure, population, period, and whether the panels share a scale.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the grid as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to every panel.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"small-multiple-grid","title":"65% of Dutch workers aged 25 to 34 worked from home usually or sometimes in 2023","subtitle":"Share of employed people working from home usually or sometimes, by age group, six EU countries, 2023. All panels run from 0 to 70%","data":[{"country":"Netherlands","age":"16-24","Usually":18,"Sometimes":22},{"country":"Netherlands","age":"25-34","Usually":44,"Sometimes":21},{"country":"Netherlands","age":"35-49","Usually":41,"Sometimes":19},{"country":"Netherlands","age":"50-64","Usually":33,"Sometimes":17},{"country":"Netherlands","age":"65+","Usually":14,"Sometimes":9},{"country":"Sweden","age":"16-24","Usually":14,"Sometimes":20},{"country":"Sweden","age":"25-34","Usually":39,"Sometimes":22},{"country":"Sweden","age":"35-49","Usually":37,"Sometimes":20}],"facet":"country","columns":3,"panelHeight":170,"legend":["Usually","Sometimes"],"chart":{"type":"bar-chart","x":"age","y":["Usually","Sometimes"],"stack":true,"sort":"none","orientation":"horizontal","format":"{value}%","labels":false,"legend":false,"option":{"xAxis":{"max":70}}},"source":"Eurostat, Labour Force Survey","note":"Rounded, illustrative"}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

### stat-row

`<StatRow>`, HTML, category layout. Two to five key figures in one row separated by hairlines, collapsing to two columns and then one as the container narrows.

Composes: `big-number`, `stat-tile`.

Props:

- `items` (required): `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format?, trend? }[]`. Two to five figures, most important first. Each takes the props of `big-number` (or `stat-tile` when `variant` is `tiles`).
- `variant`: `"plain" | "tiles"`, default `"plain"`. Open figures divided by hairlines, or bordered tiles that can carry a `trend`.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"auto"`. Number format for every figure that does not set its own.
- `title`: `string`. The main fact with its number, or a plain label.
- `subtitle`: `string`. Population and period the figures share.
- `source`: `string`. Shown under the row as "Source: ...".
- `note`: `string`. Method note or caveat.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to every figure.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode, passed on to every figure.

```json
{"type":"stat-row","title":"Renewables supplied 31.7% of the world's electricity in 2024","subtitle":"Global electricity generation, 2024","items":[{"value":0.317,"format":"percent","label":"Share from renewables","delta":"+1.9 pts","deltaLabel":"vs 2023"},{"value":2131,"label":"Solar generation, TWh","delta":0.29,"deltaLabel":"vs 2023"},{"value":2494,"label":"Wind generation, TWh","delta":0.079,"deltaLabel":"vs 2023"},{"value":0.409,"format":"percent","label":"Share from all clean sources","context":"Above 40% for the first time since the 1940s"}],"source":"Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025","note":"Figures are approximate, for illustration"}
```

### trend-card

`<TrendCard>`, HTML, category layout. A KPI card computed from a series: the latest value, its change against a baseline in the same data, and a sparkline of the series.

Composes: `stat-tile`, `sparkline`.

Props:

- `label` (required): `string`. What the figure measures, sentence case.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows in time order, one per period. Omit inside `<InsightData>`.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied to the rows before anything is computed.
- `y` (required): `string`. Value field: the series drawn and the source of the figure and its change.
- `x`: `string`. Period field, used to name the baseline and in the sparkline tooltip.
- `value`: `number | string`. The figure shown. Default: the last row's `y`.
- `delta`: `number | string`. The change shown. Default: computed from the series according to `compare`.
- `compare`: `"first" | "previous" | number`, default `"first"`. Baseline for the computed change: first row, previous row, or a number of rows back (12 for year-on-year in monthly data).
- `change`: `"percent" | "absolute"`, default `"percent"`. Relative change, or the difference between the two values (use for rates and shares). An absolute change of a percentage is shown in percentage points.
- `deltaFormat`: `FormatSpec`. Format for a computed absolute change, e.g. `"{value} pp"` or `"signed"`. Default: points ("+1.9 pts") when `format` is a percentage, otherwise `format`.
- `deltaLabel`: `string`. What the change is against. Default: "since {first period}" when `x` is given.
- `upIsGood`: `boolean`, default `true`. Whether an increase is good news; decides the delta colour.
- `context`: `string`. A line under the figure that gives it meaning.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"auto"`. Number format for the figure and the sparkline tooltip.
- `kind`: `"line" | "bar"`, default `"line"`. Sparkline form: a line for a trend, bars for discrete counts.
- `area`: `boolean`, default `false`. Light fill under the line; the scale then includes zero.
- `trendPosition`: `"bottom" | "right"`, default `"bottom"`. Where the sparkline sits; `right` falls back to `bottom` in narrow cards.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to the tile and sparkline.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode.

```json
{"type":"trend-card","label":"Monthly active users","data":[{"month":"2024-01-01","users":38100},{"month":"2024-02-01","users":39400},{"month":"2024-03-01","users":39000},{"month":"2024-04-01","users":40800},{"month":"2024-05-01","users":42200},{"month":"2024-06-01","users":41900},{"month":"2024-07-01","users":43500},{"month":"2024-08-01","users":44100}],"x":"month","y":"users","format":"compact","style":{"maxWidth":300}}
```

(`data` cut to 8 rows.)

## Templates

### atlas-poster

`<AtlasPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A landscape spread of up to eleven small illustrations of one subject, each a different graphic form, in three bands of unequal panels: a statement in large type, spokes round an icon and a network of circles; a smooth trend with its peak labelled, nested squares and a slope chart; a pill ranking, a treemap, a tile map and sized circles; and a closing row of icon statements.

Composes: `poster`, `radial-spokes`, `bubble-network`, `area-chart`, `proportional-area`, `slope-chart`, `pill-rank`, `treemap`, `choropleth-map`, `stat-circles`, `icon-stat`.

Props:

- `statement`: `{ value, label, context?, icon? }`. Band 1, left: the subject's main number in large light type, in the accent colour.
- `spokes`: `{ data, name, value, icon?, centerLabel?, highlight?, title?, ...radial-spokes props } | Slot`. Band 1, middle: 4 to 12 attributes as spokes round a centre icon (`radial-spokes`).
- `network`: `{ data, name, value, links, highlight?, tag?, title?, ...bubble-network props } | Slot`. Band 1, right: named places or things as circles sized by value and joined by lines (`bubble-network`).
- `trend`: `{ data, x, y, peak?, format?, title?, ...area-chart props } | Slot`. Band 2, wide: one measure over an ordered dimension as a smooth filled curve (`area-chart`). The highest point is labelled with its value and position; `peak` replaces that label, and `peak: false` removes it.
- `area`: `{ data, name, value, ratio?, title?, ...proportional-area props } | Slot`. Band 2: two or three quantities as squares nested from one corner, with a bracket stating the ratio (`proportional-area`, `layout: "nested"`).
- `slope`: `{ data, series, y: [from, to], names?, highlight?, title?, ...slope-chart props } | Slot`. Band 2: each entity at two dates, joined by a line and labelled at the end (`slope-chart`).
- `rank`: `{ data, name, value, highlight?, title?, ...pill-rank props } | Slot`. Band 3: a ranking of 4 to 6 rows as centred pills (`pill-rank`). Pass a `bar-chart` spec for bars instead.
- `parts`: `{ data, name, value, title?, ...treemap props } | Slot`. Band 3: the parts of one whole as tiles (`treemap`).
- `map`: `{ data, region, value, code?, geo?, title?, ...choropleth-map props } | Slot`. Band 3: a tile map shaded by value (`choropleth-map`). Give every row `col` and `row`, the tile's place in the grid, and the template builds the squares; `code` names the field printed on each tile. Pass `geo` to use your own GeoJSON.
- `circles`: `{ data, name, value, unit?, title?, ...stat-circles props } | Slot`. Band 3: two to four magnitudes as sized circles (`stat-circles`).
- `stats`: `{ count, total?, text, icon?, value? }[]`. Closing row: up to three "3 in 10" statements, each a row of icons with some filled (`icon-stat`).
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"forest"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1440`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

### comparison-brief

`<ComparisonBrief>`, HTML, category layout. A compared with B on one page. It has a headline that states the result, the headline figures mirrored either side of their labels, one hero exhibit that shows both sides, paired exhibits on a shared scale, a verdict callout and a source note.

Composes: `headline`, `prose`, `callout`, `source-note`, `line-chart`, `bar-chart`, `segmented-bar`.

Props:

- `title` (required): `string`. The result of the comparison, as one plain sentence with the number in it.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title.
- `deck`: `string`. One-sentence standfirst.
- `byline`: `string`. Author line.
- `date`: `string`. Publication date.
- `a` (required): `string | { name, detail? }`. Side A, shown on the left.
- `b` (required): `string | { name, detail? }`. Side B, shown on the right.
- `subject`: `"a" | "b" | "none"`, default `"a"`. The side the piece is about. It takes the accent colour; the other stays grey. Match it with `highlight` in the charts.
- `figures`: `{ label, a, b, format?, better?: "higher" | "lower" }[]`. Headline measures. Numeric values get mirrored bars scaled within each row; `better` sets the stronger value bolder.
- `hero`: `Slot`. The exhibit that shows both sides at once. Default height 360px.
- `heroText`: `string`. One or two sentences under the hero.
- `pairs`: `{ title, text?, a: Slot, b: Slot }[]`. Paired exhibits under one heading. A is on the left and B on the right; they stack in narrow containers. Use the same form and scale for both.
- `verdict`: `{ lead?, body?, label?, tone? }`. The closing recommendation, shown as a callout.
- `sources`: `string | { name, url? } | (string | { name, url? })[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked.
- `period`: `string`. The period the data covers.
- `method`: `string`. How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions.
- `note`: `string`. Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the piece.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `1`. Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`. Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to everything inside.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode, passed on to everything inside.


### count-poster

`<CountPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A poster that counts at scale. Blocks of thousands of unit icons fill most of the sheet, a second band counts reference groups with the same icon at the same size in a muted colour, and a bottom row holds three small graphics: squares sized by area with a ratio bracket, thick bars with the numbers inside, and shares as nested outlines or filled silhouettes.

Composes: `poster`, `unit-blocks`, `proportional-area`, `block-bar`, `nested-shares`, `shape-fill`.

Props:

- `hero` (required): `{ data, name, value, title?, subtitle?, source?, ...unit-blocks props } | Slot`. The hero band: one block of unit icons per row, drawn by `unit-blocks`. A full spec or element replaces it.
- `unit`: `number`. Units one icon stands for, in both bands. Default: a round number that gives the hero about 2,000 icons.
- `unitLabel`: `string`. What one icon stands for, e.g. "1,000 pupils". Printed as the key of both bands.
- `icon`: `IconName | "path://..."`, default `"person"`. Icon of both bands.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`, default `"integer"`. How to print the counts.
- `reference`: `{ data, name, value, title?, ... } | Slot`. The second band: reference groups counted with the same icon at the same size, painted in the theme's context grey (`unit-blocks`).
- `area`: `{ data, name, value, ratio?, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom left: two to four values as squares sized by area, with a bracket stating how many times the largest is the smallest (`proportional-area`). `ratio` defaults to `"{ratio}x larger"`.
- `bars`: `{ data, name, value, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom middle: 3 to 8 values as thick rounded bars with the numbers inside (`block-bar`).
- `shares`: `{ data, name, value, icon?, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom right: shares of one whole. With `icon` each share is a silhouette filled to its level (`shape-fill`); without, the shares are outlines nested in one square (`nested-shares`).
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"noir"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1100`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

```json
{"type":"count-poster","theme":"noir","kicker":"Education","title":"Norland's schools taught 1.84 million pupils in 2025","subtitle":"Pupils enrolled in state schools by stage, autumn term 2025.","unit":1000,"unitLabel":"1,000 people","icon":"person","hero":{"data":[{"stage":"Primary","pupils":820000},{"stage":"Lower secondary","pupils":460000},{"stage":"Upper secondary","pupils":390000},{"stage":"Vocational","pupils":170000}],"name":"stage","value":"pupils","title":"820,000 pupils were in primary school"},"reference":{"data":[{"group":"Teachers","people":142000},{"group":"Support staff","people":61000},{"group":"Pupils who left without a certificate","people":38000}],"name":"group","value":"people","title":"142,000 teachers taught them"},"area":{"data":[{"school":"Largest secondary school","pupils":3640},{"school":"Median primary school","pupils":280}],"name":"school","value":"pupils","title":"The largest school had 3,640 pupils"},"bars":{"data":[{"year":"2000","m":1.42},{"year":"2005","m":1.51},{"year":"2010","m":1.6},{"year":"2015","m":1.69},{"year":"2020","m":1.77},{"year":"2025","m":1.84}],"name":"year","value":"m","format":"{value}m","title":"Enrolment was 1.42 million in 2000"},"shares":{"data":[{"year":"2013","share":6},{"year":"2017","share":19},{"year":"2021","share":44},{"year":"2025","share":68}],"name":"year","value":"share","highlight":"2025","wholeLabel":"All pupils","title":"68% of pupils had a school laptop in 2025"},"sources":"Norland Ministry of Education, school census 2025","note":"Norland is an invented country. All figures are illustrative.","credit":"InsightCharts"}
```

### data-explorer

`<DataExplorer>`, HTML, category story. A set of linked charts over one shared dataset that filter each other. It has a headline, a sentence of instructions with filter chips, a row of figures that recompute from the filtered rows, two to four charts and an optional detail table. It opens on selections the author chooses.

Composes: `headline`, `callout`, `filter-chips`, `stat-row`, `linked-charts`, `data-table`, `source-note`, `bar-chart`.

Props:

- `title` (required): `string`. What the starting view shows, as one plain sentence with the number in it.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title.
- `deck`: `string`. One-sentence standfirst.
- `byline`: `string`. Author line.
- `date`: `string`. Publication date.
- `instructions`: `string`. One sentence saying what can be clicked and what happens. Shown in the filter line.
- `finding`: `{ lead?, body?, label? }`. A callout saying what to look for in the starting view.
- `data` (required): `DataInput`. The shared, row-level dataset: rows, CSV text, a URL or a loader.
- `transform`: `Transform | Transform[]`. Applied once to the shared data.
- `charts` (required): `Slot[]`. Two to four chart specs. Give each a stable `id`, `select: true` (or a field name) and its own aggregating `transform`; leave out `data`.
- `initialSelections`: `Record<string, { field, values?, range? }>`. Selections the piece opens with, keyed by chart `id`. A button restores them after the reader changes the filter.
- `figures`: `{ label, field?, op?, where?: { field, value }, per?, format?, context? }[]`. Figures recomputed from the filtered rows: `op` over `field` (default sum; count without a field), optionally restricted by `where` and divided by the sum of `per` for a rate or share. While a filter is active each shows the all-rows value as context.
- `table`: `{ transform?, columns?, caption?, sort?, highlight?, ... }`. A detail table of the filtered rows: the props of `data-table` without `rows`, plus a `transform` applied first.
- `labels`: `Record<string, string>`. Display names for fields in the filter chips.
- `unit`: `string`, default `"rows"`. Noun for what the figures total, used in figure context ("3,650 across all trips").
- `count`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show the filtered row count beside the chips.
- `rowUnit`: `string`, default `"rows"`. Noun for one row of `data` in that count.
- `columns`: `number`. Preferred chart columns.
- `restoreLabel`: `string`, default `"Back to the starting view"`. Label of the button that restores `initialSelections`.
- `sources`: `string | { name, url? } | (string | { name, url? })[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked.
- `period`: `string`. The period the data covers.
- `method`: `string`. How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions.
- `note`: `string`. Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the piece.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `1`. Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`. Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to everything inside.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode, passed on to everything inside.

### executive-brief

`<ExecutiveBrief>`, HTML, category layout. A one-page summary. It has a headline that states the main finding with its number, a deck, a row of three or four key figures, one hero chart with a takeaway callout, two smaller supporting exhibits, a short list of actions and a source note.

Composes: `headline`, `stat-row`, `chart-callout`, `prose`, `source-note`, `line-chart`, `dumbbell-chart`, `bar-chart`.

Props:

- `title` (required): `string`. The main finding, as one plain sentence with the number and the period in it.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the report series or team.
- `deck`: `string`. One to three short sentences. Each states one more fact.
- `byline`: `string`. Author line, shown as written.
- `date`: `string`. Publication date. ISO dates are formatted for the locale.
- `figures`: `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format? }[]`. Three or four key figures, most important first. Rendered with `stat-row`.
- `hero` (required): `Slot`. The hero exhibit: a chart spec or element whose `title` states one fact with its number. Gets a height of 340px (260px on phones) unless it sets one.
- `takeaway`: `{ lead?, body?, label?, tone? }`. The callout beside the hero. `lead` is one short sentence stating the main fact. `body` gives the supporting numbers.
- `supporting`: `Slot[]`. Two (at most three) smaller exhibits shown side by side; they stack in narrow containers. Default height 220px.
- `actions`: `(string | { title, text?, owner? })[]`. Recommended actions, numbered. Two to four.
- `actionsTitle`: `string`, default `"What to do"`. Heading of the actions list.
- `sources`: `string | { name, url? } | (string | { name, url? })[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked.
- `period`: `string`. The period the data covers.
- `method`: `string`. How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions.
- `note`: `string`. Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the piece.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `1`. Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`. Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to everything inside.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode, passed on to everything inside.

### explainer

`<Explainer>`, HTML, category story. A vertical infographic in one narrow column. It opens with a big number or a proportion statement (`hook`), then the hero exhibit, then numbered sections with one exhibit each, a conclusion with an optional link, and sources.

Composes: `headline`, `big-number`, `proportion-statement`, `step-marker`, `prose`, `callout`, `source-note`, `bar-chart`, `icon-stat`, `line-chart`, `segmented-bar`.

Props:

- `title` (required): `string`. The main finding, as one plain sentence with the number and the period in it.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title.
- `deck`: `string`. One-sentence standfirst.
- `byline`: `string`. Author line.
- `date`: `string`. Publication date.
- `hook`: `{ value, total?, text?, figure?, visual?, icon?, detail?, label?, context?, format? } | Slot`. The opening number. With `text` it renders a `proportion-statement` ("19 in every 100 ..."); with `label` a hero `big-number`. A spec or element is rendered as given.
- `hero`: `Slot`. The main exhibit. Its `title` states one fact with its number. Default height 360px.
- `heroText`: `string`. One or two sentences under the hero. Each states one more fact.
- `sections`: `{ title, text?, exhibit?, takeaway?, id? }[]`. Numbered sections. Each has a heading, one exhibit and a `takeaway` sentence with its main number.
- `screenful`: `boolean`, default `false`. Give every section at least the height of the viewport and centre its content, so each fills a screen.
- `conclusion`: `{ title, text?, points?, action?: { label, href } }`. The closing block: a heading, text, a list of actions and an optional link.
- `sources`: `string | { name, url? } | (string | { name, url? })[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked.
- `period`: `string`. The period the data covers.
- `method`: `string`. How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions.
- `note`: `string`. Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the piece.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `1`. Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`. Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers.
- `theme`: `ThemeInput`. Theme override, passed on to everything inside.
- `mode`: `"auto" | "system" | "light" | "dark"`, default `"auto"`. Colour mode, passed on to everything inside.

### flow-poster

`<FlowPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A portrait poster of where something comes from and where it goes, in three stacked bands painted in one colour: the producers as large labelled tiles, the leading producer's output fanning out as ribbons to an aligned column of destinations, and the destinations as bubbles on a scale of how much each depends on that producer.

Composes: `poster`, `treemap`, `fan-flow`, `bubble-scale`.

Props:

- `producers` (required): `{ data, name, value, title?, subtitle?, source?, ...treemap props } | Slot`. Top band: the producers as tiles sized by output (`treemap`). The leading one is painted in the accent.
- `lead`: `string`. The producer the flow starts from. Default: the largest row of `producers`. It names the block the ribbons leave.
- `flow` (required): `{ data, name, value, trunk?, tagged?, tagLabel?, title?, ...fan-flow props } | Slot`. Middle band: one ribbon per destination, as thick as its value, ending at a column of names, values and shares (`fan-flow`).
- `scale`: `{ data, name, value, size, scaleLabel?, sizeFormat?, title?, ...bubble-scale props } | Slot`. Bottom band: one bubble per destination, placed by `value` on a 0 to 100 scale and sized by `size` (`bubble-scale`). Set `domain` and `ticks` for a scale that is not a percentage.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`. How to print the quantities of the top and middle bands, e.g. `"{value} kt"`.
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"magenta"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `920`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

```json
{"type":"flow-poster","theme":"magenta","kicker":"Fishing","title":"Six ports on the Verran Coast landed 412,000 tonnes of fish in 2025","subtitle":"Landings by port, the buyers of Port Alda's catch, and how much each buyer relies on Port Alda. Thousand tonnes (kt).","format":"{value} kt","producers":{"data":[{"port":"Port Alda","kt":148},{"port":"Skerry","kt":96},{"port":"Marrow Bay","kt":71},{"port":"Tolven","kt":52},{"port":"Hask","kt":28},{"port":"Lund","kt":17}],"name":"port","value":"kt","title":"Port Alda landed 148,000 of the 412,000 tonnes"},"flow":{"data":[{"buyer":"Canneries","kt":46},{"buyer":"Fresh markets","kt":34},{"buyer":"Frozen export","kt":29},{"buyer":"Fishmeal plants","kt":21},{"buyer":"Restaurants","kt":11},{"buyer":"Smokehouses","kt":7}],"name":"buyer","value":"kt","trunk":"Port Alda","title":"Canneries bought 46,000 tonnes of Port Alda's catch"},"scale":{"data":[{"buyer":"Canneries","fromAlda":56,"kt":82},{"buyer":"Fresh markets","fromAlda":35,"kt":96},{"buyer":"Frozen export","fromAlda":23,"kt":124},{"buyer":"Fishmeal plants","fromAlda":34,"kt":61},{"buyer":"Restaurants","fromAlda":29,"kt":38},{"buyer":"Smokehouses","fromAlda":64,"kt":11}],"name":"buyer","value":"fromAlda","size":"kt","sizeFormat":"{value} kt","scaleLabel":"From Port Alda","title":"Smokehouses bought 64% of their fish from Port Alda","subtitle":"Share of each buyer's fish landed at Port Alda (position) and all the fish it bought (area)"},"sources":"Verran Coast Fisheries Board landing returns","note":"The Verran Coast is an invented place. All figures are illustrative.","credit":"InsightCharts"}
```

### matrix-poster

`<MatrixPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. One wide landscape graphic that compares 4 to 12 entities on five to seven measures: two measures as S-curves between parallel scales on the left, joined to a table on the right in which every other number is drawn as dots, squares, icons, a ring, a circle or a bar. Both halves share one row order and one colour per entity.

Composes: `poster`, `curve-rank`, `glyph-table`.

Props:

- `rows` (required): `Row[]`. One object per entity, holding the name and every measure.
- `name`: `string`. Field holding the entity name. Default: the first key of the first row.
- `nameLabel`: `string`. Heading of the table's name column.
- `curve` (required): `{ left, right, leftLabel?, rightLabel?, leftFormat?, rightFormat?, leftTop?, rightTop?, title?, subtitle?, source?, ...curve-rank props }`. Left graphic: the two measures joined by one S-curve per entity (`curve-rank`). The poster's rows are ordered by `left`, largest first.
- `columns` (required): `{ field, label?, glyph?, unit?, format?, max?, icon? }[]`. Right graphic: the glyph columns of the table, in order (`glyph-table`). Three to five read well beside the curves.
- `table`: `{ title?, subtitle?, source?, note? }`. Short heading and source line over and under the table.
- `order`: `string[]`. Entity names in display order, for both graphics. Default: largest first on the curve's left measure.
- `highlight`: `string | string[]`. Entities drawn in colour while every other one turns grey. Without it each entity has its own colour in both graphics.
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"paper"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1400`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

### network-poster

`<NetworkPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A poster of who is connected to whom: a full-width arc diagram with one arc per connection, as thick as its value (`arc-diagram`), a strip of two to four large figures, and a bottom row where the same entities return as circles joined by lines (`bubble-network`) and as a ranking of centred pills (`pill-rank`).

Composes: `poster`, `arc-diagram`, `bubble-network`, `pill-rank`.

Props:

- `hero` (required): `{ data, from, to, value?, order?, colorBy?, arcLabels?, orientation?, format?, highlight?, title?, ... } | Slot`. The hero: one arc per pair of connected entities, drawn by `arc-diagram`. Rows joining the same pair are summed. A full spec or element replaces it.
- `figures`: `{ value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string; tag?: string }[]`. Two to four large figures in a strip under the hero.
- `map`: `{ data, name, value, links?, x?, y?, layout?, tag?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom left: the entities as circles sized by `value` and joined by `links: { from, to, value? }[]` (`bubble-network`). `x` and `y` (0 to 100) place the circles by hand.
- `rank`: `{ data, name, value, highlight?, compare?, format?, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom right: the entities ranked by one measure as centred pills (`pill-rank`). With only one of `map` and `rank`, that one takes the full width.
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"dusk"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1100`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

### profile-poster

`<ProfilePoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A poster that describes one subject from four sides: the subject as one large silhouette filled to a share (`shape-fill`), two to four large figures, its place among other things on one scale (`scale-ladder`), and a table that sets it beside its peers with every number drawn as a small form (`glyph-table`).

Composes: `poster`, `shape-fill`, `scale-ladder`, `glyph-table`.

Props:

- `portrait` (required): `{ data, name, value, icon, max?, format?, title?, ... } | Slot`. The portrait: one silhouette filled from the bottom to the share in its row, with the number beside it, drawn by `shape-fill`. `format` defaults to `"{value}%"`. A full spec or element replaces it.
- `figures`: `{ value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string; tag?: string }[]`. Two to four large figures about the subject. In the three-column layout they stand between the silhouette and the scale; otherwise they run in a strip.
- `scale`: `{ data, name, value, iconField?, direction?, scale?, min?, max?, zones?, scaleLabel?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } | Slot`. The subject among 4 to 10 other things on one scale (`scale-ladder`). It is drawn as tall as the silhouette.
- `table`: `{ rows, name, columns, nameLabel?, highlight?, order?, title?, ... } | Slot`. The subject beside its peers, one row each, with a glyph per measure (`glyph-table`). `columns` is `{ field, label?, glyph?, unit?, format?, max?, icon? }[]`.
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"blueprint"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1100`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

### radial-poster

`<RadialPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A poster with one subject in the middle of the sheet: a wheel of spokes round an icon (`radial-spokes`), two to four large figures standing either side of it, and a bottom row with the same subject's surroundings on concentric rings (`orbit-chart`) and a ranking as centred pills (`pill-rank`).

Composes: `poster`, `radial-spokes`, `orbit-chart`, `pill-rank`.

Props:

- `hero` (required): `{ data, name, value, icon?, centerLabel?, shape?, sweep?, max?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } | Slot`. The hero: one spoke per row round a centre disc, drawn by `radial-spokes`. A full spec or element replaces it.
- `figures`: `{ value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string; tag?: string }[]`. Two to four large figures. On a sheet at least 960px wide they stand in two columns either side of the hero; on a narrower one they run in a row under it.
- `rings`: `{ data, name, ring, value?, rings?, ringLabel?, sizeLabel?, icon?, centerLabel?, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom left: named things on concentric rings, one ring per category, level or period (`orbit-chart`).
- `rank`: `{ data, name, value, highlight?, compare?, format?, title?, ... } | Slot`. Bottom right: a ranking as centred pills (`pill-rank`). With only one of `rings` and `rank`, that one takes the full width.
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"magenta"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1100`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.

### ranking-poster

`<RankingPoster>`, HTML, category infographic. A poster of one subject by the numbers, in four rows: two figures in large type or as filled silhouettes, two treemaps side by side, a full-width ranking of centred pills with one row highlighted, and packed circles with icons beside a column of sized circles and a closing figure.

Composes: `poster`, `shape-fill`, `treemap`, `pill-rank`, `circle-pack`, `stat-circles`.

Props:

- `figures`: `({ value, label, context?, icon? } | { data, name, value, icon, title?, ...shape-fill props } | Slot)[]`. Top row, up to two. A statement `{ value, label }` is set in large light type (the first in the accent colour); a config with `data` draws silhouettes filled to their level (`shape-fill`).
- `breakdowns`: `({ data, name, value, title?, ...treemap props } | Slot)[]`. Second row, up to two: the subject's total split two ways, as treemaps side by side.
- `ranking` (required): `{ data, name, value, highlight?, compare?, compareLabel?, title?, ...pill-rank props } | Slot`. Third row, full width: a ranking as centred pills with the value at the left and the rank at the right (`pill-rank`). `highlight` names the row drawn in the accent.
- `pack`: `{ data, name, value, icon?, group?, title?, ...circle-pack props } | Slot`. Bottom left: parts as packed circles (`circle-pack`). `icon` is one icon name or a map from circle name to icon.
- `circles`: `{ data, name, value, unit?, title?, ...stat-circles props } | Slot`. Bottom right: two to four related magnitudes as circles standing on one baseline (`stat-circles`).
- `figure`: `{ value, label, context?, icon? }`. Bottom right, under the circles: one closing figure in large type.
- `format`: `FormatSpec`. How to print values in the regions that set no `format` of their own.
- `title` (required): `string`. The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number.
- `kicker`: `string`. Small label above the title: the topic.
- `subtitle`: `string`. One line under the title: the measure, population and period.
- `theme`: `PosterThemeName | string | ThemeInput`, default `"dusk"`. Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object.
- `mode`: `"light" | "dark" | "auto" | "system"`, default `"light"`. Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- `download`: `boolean`, default `false`. Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image.
- `maxWidth`: `number | string`, default `1100`. Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers.
- `linked`: `boolean`, default `false`. Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear.
- `data`: `DataInput`. Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions.
- `sources`: `string | string[]`. Where the data comes from, shown in the footer.
- `note`: `string`. Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data".
- `credit`: `string`. Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer.
- `level`: `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5`, default `2`. Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down.
